title.zh: 卷84 儒林:梁越 盧醜 張偉 梁祚 平恆 陳奇 常爽 劉獻之
title.en: Volume 84: Renowned Confucians - Liang Yue, Lu Chou, Zhang Wei, Liang Zuo, Ping Heng, Chen Qi, Chang Shuang, Liu Xianzhi
title.raw: 卷84 儒林:梁越 盧醜 張偉 梁祚 平恆 陳奇 常爽 劉獻之 Volume 84: Renowned Confucians - Liang Yue, Lu Chou, Zhang Wei, Liang Zuo, Ping Heng, Chen Qi, Chang Shuang, Liu Xianzhi

sentences.zh: 梁越 盧醜 張偉 梁祚 平恒 陳奇 常爽 劉獻之 張吾貴 劉蘭 孫惠蔚 徐遵明 董徵 刁沖 盧景裕 李同軌 李業興

translations.literal: Liang Yue, Lu Chou, Zhang Wei, Liang Zuo, Ping Heng, Chen Qi, Chang Shuang, Liu Xianzhi, Zhang Wugui, Liu Lan, Sun Huiwei, Xu Zunming, Dong Zheng, Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, Li Tonggui, Li Yexing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yue, Lu Chou, Zhang Wei, Liang Zuo, Ping Heng, Chen Qi, Chang Shuang, Liu Xianzhi, Zhang Wugui, Liu Lan, Sun Huiwei, Xu Zunming, Dong Zheng, Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, Li Tonggui, and Li Yexing.

sentences.zh: 自晉永嘉之後，運鍾喪亂，宇內分崩，羣凶肆禍，生民不見俎豆之容，黔首唯覩戎馬之跡，禮樂文章，掃地將盡。

translations.literal: From after the Yongjia era of Jin, the age met with ruin and disorder; within the four seas the realm split apart, many villains unleashed calamity, the living people did not see the appearance of sacrificial vessels, the common folk only beheld the tracks of war-horses, and ritual, music, and literature were swept away, nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongjia reign of the Jin, the times turned to ruin and chaos. The realm shattered within the four seas, villains ran rampant, and the people no longer saw ritual vessels set out—commoners saw only the hoofprints of war-horses. Ritual, music, and learning were all but swept from the earth.

sentences.zh: 而契之所感，斯道猶存。

translations.literal: Yet what Qi was moved by—this Way still remained.
translations.idiomatic: Yet through what moved Qi, this tradition still endured.

sentences.zh: 高才有德之流，自強蓬蓽；

translations.literal: The stream of men of lofty talent and virtue strengthened themselves amid thatched huts;
translations.idiomatic: Men of outstanding talent and virtue strengthened themselves in humble dwellings;

sentences.zh: 鴻生碩儒之輩，抱器晦己。

translations.literal: the company of great scholars and eminent Confucians held their learning and hid themselves.
translations.idiomatic: while great scholars and eminent Confucians cherished their learning and kept themselves in obscurity.

sentences.zh: 太祖初定中原，雖日不暇給，始建都邑，便以經術為先，立太學，置五經博士生員千有餘人。

translations.literal: When the Taizu first secured the Central Plains, though each day allowed no respite, as soon as he founded the capital he put the classics first, established the Imperial Academy, and appointed more than a thousand students for the Five Classics doctoral chairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daowu first pacified the Central Plains, though his days left no spare moment, he founded his capital and at once made the classics his priority: he established the Imperial Academy and enrolled more than a thousand students under the Five Classics doctoral chairs.

sentences.zh: 天興二年春，增國子太學生員至三千。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Tianxing, the number of National University and Imperial Academy students was increased to three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Tianxing, enrollment at the National University and Imperial Academy was raised to three thousand.

sentences.zh: 豈不以天下可馬上取之，不可以馬上治之，為國之道，文武兼用，毓才成務，意在茲乎？

translations.literal: Was it not because the realm may be taken on horseback but cannot be governed on horseback—that the way to rule a state employs both civil and military arts together, nurtures talent to accomplish tasks, and the intent lay herein?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not because an empire may be won from horseback but cannot be ruled from horseback—that sound governance requires both civil and military cultivation, nurturing talent to accomplish the work of state? The meaning lay precisely here.

sentences.zh: 聖達經猷，蓋為遠矣。

translations.literal: The sagely penetration of the classics' design was, it seems, far-reaching indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Such sagely grasp of the classics' design reached far indeed.

sentences.zh: 四年春，命樂師入學習舞，釋菜于先聖、先師。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, he ordered music masters to enter the school to study the dances and performed the vegetable-offering rite before the former sages and former teachers.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he ordered music masters into the academy to learn the ritual dances and offered the vegetable sacrifice to the former sages and teachers.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，改國子為中書學，立教授博士。

translations.literal: In the age of Taizong, the National University was changed to the Secretariat School, and instructing professors and doctoral chairs were established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Mingyuan, the National University was renamed the Secretariat School, with instructing professors and doctoral chairs appointed.

sentences.zh: 世祖始光三年春，別起太學於城東，後徵盧玄、高允等，而令州郡各舉才學。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Shiguang under Shizu, a separate Imperial Academy was raised east of the city; later Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and others were summoned, and the commanderies and prefectures were each ordered to recommend men of talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Shiguang under Emperor Taiwu, a new Imperial Academy was built east of the city. Later Lu Xuan, Gao Yun, and others were summoned, and every prefecture and commandery was ordered to recommend men of learning and ability.

sentences.zh: 於是人多砥尚，儒林轉興。

translations.literal: Thereupon many people sharpened their aspirations, and the forest of scholars flourished anew.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon many took up the pursuit of learning, and Confucian studies revived.

sentences.zh: 顯祖天安初，詔立鄉學，郡置博士二人，助教二人，學生六十人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tian'an under Xianzu, an edict established district schools: each commandery was to have two doctoral chairs, two teaching assistants, and sixty students.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tian'an under Emperor Xianwen, an edict established district schools, each commandery appointing two doctoral chairs, two teaching assistants, and sixty students.

sentences.zh: 後詔：大郡立博士二人，助教四人，學生一百人；

translations.literal: Later an edict stated: large commanderies were to establish two doctoral chairs, four teaching assistants, and one hundred students;
translations.idiomatic: A later edict specified: large commanderies were to have two doctoral chairs, four teaching assistants, and one hundred students;

sentences.zh: 次郡立博士二人，助教二人，學生八十人；

translations.literal: secondary commanderies two doctoral chairs, two teaching assistants, and eighty students;
translations.idiomatic: secondary commanderies two doctoral chairs, two teaching assistants, and eighty students;

sentences.zh: 中郡立博士一人，助教二人，學生六十人；

translations.literal: middle commanderies one doctoral chair, two teaching assistants, and sixty students;
translations.idiomatic: middle commanderies one doctoral chair, two teaching assistants, and sixty students;

sentences.zh: 下郡立博士一人，助教一人，學生四十人。

translations.literal: small commanderies one doctoral chair, one teaching assistant, and forty students.
translations.idiomatic: and small commanderies one doctoral chair, one teaching assistant, and forty students.

sentences.zh: 太和中，改中書學為國子學，建明堂辟雍，尊三老五更，又開皇子之學。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, the Secretariat School was changed back to the National University; the Bright Hall and Imperial Academy were built; the Three Elders and Five More Venerable were honored; and schooling for imperial princes was also opened.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era the Secretariat School was restored as the National University. The Bright Hall and Imperial Academy were built, the Three Elders and Five More Venerable were honored, and instruction for imperial princes was instituted.

sentences.zh: 及遷都洛邑，詔立國子太學、四門小學。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Luoyang, an edict established the National University, Imperial Academy, and Four Gates Elementary School.
translations.idiomatic: When the court moved the capital to Luoyang, an edict established the National University, Imperial Academy, and Four Gates Elementary School.

sentences.zh: 高祖欽明稽古，篤好墳典，坐輿據鞍，不忘講道。

translations.literal: Gaozu was reverently clear in examining antiquity, deeply fond of the ancient texts; whether seated in a carriage or mounted on a saddle, he did not forget to discuss the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen was reverently devoted to antiquity and deeply loved the ancient classics; whether in his carriage or on horseback, he never ceased discussing the classics.

sentences.zh: 劉芳、李彪諸人以經書進，崔光、邢巒之徒以文史達，其餘涉獵典章，關歷詞翰，莫不縻以好爵，動貽賞眷。

translations.literal: Liu Fang, Li Biao, and others advanced through the classics; Cui Guang, Xing Luan, and their kind attained office through letters and histories; the rest who ranged through statutes and regulations or passed through literary composition—all without exception were bound with fine ranks, and movement brought rewards and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fang, Li Biao, and others rose through mastery of the classics; Cui Guang, Xing Luan, and their peers through letters and histories; and all who ranged through statutes or excelled in literary composition were rewarded with fine offices and imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 於是斯文鬱然，比隆周漢。

translations.literal: Thereupon cultured writing flourished luxuriantly, rivaling the glory of Zhou and Han.
translations.idiomatic: Thus learning flourished abundantly, rivaling the heights of the Zhou and Han.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，復詔營國學，樹小學於四門，大選儒生，以為小學博士，員四十人。

translations.literal: In the time of Shizong, an edict again ordered construction of the National University, established elementary schools at the Four Gates, made a great selection of Confucian scholars to serve as elementary-school doctoral chairs—forty posts in all.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu an edict again ordered the National University rebuilt and elementary schools established at the Four Gates. A great selection of Confucian scholars was made to serve as elementary-school doctoral chairs—forty in all.

sentences.zh: 雖黌宇未立，而經術彌顯。

translations.literal: Although the school buildings were not yet completed, the classics' learning grew ever more manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Though the school buildings were not yet finished, study of the classics grew ever more prominent.

sentences.zh: 時天下承平，學業大盛。

translations.literal: At the time the realm enjoyed peace, and scholarly pursuit greatly flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was at peace, and learning flourished as never before.

sentences.zh: 故燕齊趙魏之間，橫經著錄，不可勝數。

translations.literal: Thus between Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei, those who stretched out the classics and were recorded could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yan, Qi, Zhao, and Wei, scholars who lectured on the classics and were recorded in the rolls were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 大者千餘人，小者猶數百。

translations.literal: The largest had more than a thousand; the smallest still had several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The largest schools had more than a thousand students; even the smallest had several hundred.

sentences.zh: 州舉茂異，郡貢孝廉，對揚王庭，每年逾眾。

translations.literal: Prefectures recommended outstanding talent, commanderies presented Filial and Incorrupt candidates, and those who answered and expounded before the royal court grew in number each year.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures recommended outstanding men, commanderies presented Filial and Incorrupt candidates, and those who appeared before the throne to expound the classics increased in number year by year.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，將立國學，詔以三品已上及五品清官之子以充生選。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era, as the National University was about to be established, an edict ordered that sons of officials of the third rank and above and of fifth-rank pure offices should fill the student selections.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui era, when the National University was about to be established, an edict specified that sons of third-rank officials and above and of fifth-rank pure offices should be selected as students.

sentences.zh: 未及簡置，仍復停寢。

translations.literal: Before the selection could be completed, it was again suspended.
translations.idiomatic: Before the selection could be carried out, the plan was suspended once more.

sentences.zh: 正光二年，乃釋奠於國學，命祭酒崔光講孝經，始置國子生三十六人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengguang, the libation sacrifice was finally performed at the National University; the libationer Cui Guang was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, and thirty-six National University students were first appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengguang the libation sacrifice was held at the National University. Libationer Cui Guang was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, and thirty-six National University students were appointed for the first time.

sentences.zh: 暨孝昌之後，海內淆亂，四方校學所存無幾。

translations.literal: After Xiaochang, within the seas there was turmoil, and of the schools in the four directions scarcely any remained.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xiaochang era the realm fell into chaos, and few schools survived anywhere in the empire.

sentences.zh: 永熙中，復釋奠於國學；

translations.literal: In the Yongxi era, the libation sacrifice was again performed at the National University;
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era the libation sacrifice was again held at the National University;

sentences.zh: 又於顯陽殿詔祭酒劉廞講孝經，黃門李郁說禮記，中書舍人盧景宣講大戴禮夏小正篇；

translations.literal: also at the Xianyang Hall an edict ordered Libationer Liu Yin to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Huangmen Attendant Li Yu to expound the Record of Rites, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Jingxuan to lecture on the Xiaozheng chapter of the Elder Dai's Record of Rites;
translations.idiomatic: and at the Xianyang Hall Libationer Liu Yin was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Huangmen Attendant Li Yu to expound the Record of Rites, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Jingxuan to lecture on the Xiaozheng chapter of the Elder Dai's Record of Rites;

sentences.zh: 復置生七十二人。

translations.literal: seventy-two students were again appointed.
translations.idiomatic: seventy-two students were again enrolled.

sentences.zh: 及遷都於鄴，國子置生三十六人。

translations.literal: When the capital was moved to Ye, the National University appointed thirty-six students.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was moved to Ye, the National University enrolled thirty-six students.

sentences.zh: 至於興和、武定之世，寇難既平，儒業復光矣。

translations.literal: By the ages of Xinghe and Wuding, once the raids and hardships had been pacified, Confucian learning shone forth again.
translations.idiomatic: By the Xinghe and Wuding eras, once the wars had ended, Confucian learning flourished once more.

sentences.zh: 漢世鄭玄並為眾經注解，服虔、何休各有所說。

translations.literal: In Han times Zheng Xuan annotated all the classics together; Fu Qian and He Xiu each had his own explanations.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Zheng Xuan annotated the classics comprehensively, while Fu Qian and He Xiu each had his own school of interpretation.

sentences.zh: 玄易、書、詩、禮、論語、孝經，虔左氏春秋，休公羊傳，大行於河北。

translations.literal: Xuan's commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety, Fu's Zuo Commentary on the Spring and Autumn, and He's Gongyang Commentary were greatly practiced north of the Yellow River.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's commentaries on the Changes, Documents, Odes, Rites, Analects, and Classic of Filial Piety, Fu's Zuo Commentary, and He's Gongyang Commentary all flourished north of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 王肅易亦間行焉。

translations.literal: Wang Su's commentary on the Changes also circulated there from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Su's commentary on the Changes also circulated there occasionally.

sentences.zh: 晉世杜預注左氏，預玄孫坦、坦弟驥於劉義隆世並為青州刺史，傳其家業，故齊地多習之。

translations.literal: In Jin times Du Yu annotated the Zuo Commentary; Yu's great-great-grandson Tan and Tan's younger brother Ji, both serving as Qingzhou governors in the age of Liu Yilong, transmitted the family learning, and therefore the Qi region largely studied it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin times Du Yu annotated the Zuo Commentary. His great-great-grandsons Tan and Ji both served as Qingzhou governors under Liu Yilong and transmitted the family tradition, so the Qi region largely followed Du Yu's school.

sentences.zh: 自梁越以下傳受講說者甚眾。

translations.literal: From Liang Yue downward, those who transmitted and received lectures and explanations were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: From Liang Yue onward, those who transmitted and taught these traditions were exceedingly numerous.

sentences.zh: 今舉其知名者附列於後云。

translations.literal: Now their well-known names are listed and appended below.
translations.idiomatic: The well-known among them are listed below.

sentences.zh: 梁越，字玄覽，新興人也。

translations.literal: Liang Yue, styled Xuanlan, was a man of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Yue, courtesy name Xuanlan, was a native of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 少而好學，博綜經傳，無所不通。

translations.literal: From youth he loved learning, broadly mastered the classics and their traditions, and had nothing he did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he loved learning and mastered the classics and their commentaries comprehensively.

sentences.zh: 性純和篤信，行無擇善。

translations.literal: His nature was pure, harmonious, and deeply faithful; in conduct he did not choose between good acts.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was pure, gentle, and deeply sincere; in conduct he never failed to do what was right.

sentences.zh: 國初為禮經博士。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state he became doctoral chair in the Rites classic.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the dynasty he served as doctoral chair in the Rites.

sentences.zh: 太祖以其謹厚，舉動可則，拜上大夫，命授諸皇子經書。

translations.literal: The Taizu, because of his prudence and solidity and because his conduct could serve as a model, appointed him Grand Master and ordered him to instruct the imperial princes in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu, finding him prudent and steadfast and his conduct worthy of emulation, appointed him Grand Master and ordered him to instruct the imperial princes in the classics.

sentences.zh: 太宗即祚，以師傅之恩賜爵祝阿侯。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, in recognition of his service as tutor he was granted the title Marquis of Zhu'a.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingyuan ascended the throne, Yue was enfeoffed as Marquis of Zhu'a in gratitude for his service as tutor.

sentences.zh: 後出為雁門太守，獲白雀以獻，拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Administrator of Yanmen, presented a white sparrow he had obtained, and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Administrator of Yanmen, presented a white sparrow he had captured, and was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子弼，早卒。

translations.literal: His son Bi died young.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bi died young.

sentences.zh: 弼子恭，襲。

translations.literal: Bi's son Gong inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Bi's son Gong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 降為雲中子。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Viscount of Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The title was reduced to Viscount of Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 無子，爵除。

translations.literal: He had no son, and the title was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He had no heir, and the title lapsed.

sentences.zh: 盧醜，昌黎徒河人，襄城王魯元之族也。

translations.literal: Lu Chou was a man of Tuhe in Changli, of the same clan as Prince of Xiangcheng Lu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chou was a native of Tuhe in Changli and a kinsman of Prince Lu Yuan of Xiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 世祖之為監國，醜以篤學博聞入授世祖經。

translations.literal: When Shizu was Heir Apparent, Chou, for his devoted learning and broad knowledge, entered to instruct the Heir in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu was crown prince, Chou was summoned for his devoted scholarship and broad learning to instruct the prince in the classics.

sentences.zh: 後以師傅舊恩賜爵濟陰公。

translations.literal: Later, in recognition of his former service as tutor, he was granted the title Duke of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was enfeoffed as Duke of Jiyin in recognition of his former service as tutor.

sentences.zh: 除鎮軍將軍，拜尚書，加散騎常侍，出為河內太守。

translations.literal: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army, made Minister, given the additional title Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and sent out as Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General Who Pacifies the Army and Minister, given the additional title Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and later served as Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 延和二年冬卒。

translations.literal: He died in the winter of the second year of Yanhe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the winter of the second year of Yanhe.

translations.literal: Text lacuna in the manuscript.
translations.idiomatic: Text lacuna in the manuscript.

sentences.zh: 初，中山襲爵，太和中，以老疾自免。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhongshan inherited the title; in the Taihe era, on account of age and illness he resigned of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhongshan had inherited the title; during the Taihe era he resigned on account of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 子升頭，襲爵，後例降。

translations.literal: His son Sheng'tou inherited the title and was later demoted by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sheng'tou inherited the title and was later demoted by regulation.

sentences.zh: 張偉，字仲業，小名翠螭，太原中都人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Wei, styled Zhongye, pet name Cuichi, was a man of Zhongdu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wei, courtesy name Zhongye, childhood name Cuichi, was a native of Zhongdu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 高祖敏，晉祕書監。

translations.literal: His ancestor Min was Jin Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestor Min had been Director of the Secretariat under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 偉學通諸經，講授鄉里，受業者常數百人。

translations.literal: Wei mastered all the classics in his learning, lectured in his home district, and those who received his instruction often numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Wei mastered all the classics and lectured in his home district, where his students often numbered several hundred.

sentences.zh: 儒謹汎納，勤於教訓，雖有頑固不曉，問至數十，偉告喻殷勤，曾無慍色。

translations.literal: Confucian, prudent, broadly accepting, diligent in instruction—even when there were the stubborn who did not understand, though questioned dozens of times, Wei explained with earnest care and never once showed anger.
translations.idiomatic: Confucian in bearing, prudent and broadly tolerant, he was tireless in teaching. Even when dull students failed to understand after being questioned dozens of times, Wei explained with patient care and never showed irritation.

sentences.zh: 常依附經典，教以孝悌，門人感其仁化，事之如父。

translations.literal: He always relied on the classics, teaching filial piety and brotherly duty; his disciples, moved by his humane transforming influence, served him as they would a father.
translations.idiomatic: He always grounded his teaching in the classics, instructing students in filial piety and brotherly duty. His disciples, moved by his humane influence, treated him as they would a father.

sentences.zh: 性恬平，不以夷嶮易操，清雅篤慎，非法不言。

translations.literal: His nature was tranquil and even; he did not alter his conduct for ease or hardship; refined, pure, deeply prudent—what was not lawful he did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was tranquil and even; he did not alter his conduct for prosperity or adversity. Refined and deeply prudent, he spoke only what was proper.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，與高允等俱被辟命，拜中書博士。

translations.literal: In the time of Shizu, together with Gao Yun and others he received summons and was appointed Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taiwu he was summoned with Gao Yun and others and appointed Doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 轉侍郎、大將軍樂安王範從事中郎、馮翊太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant, Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Grand General, Prince of Le'an Fan, and Administrator of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman Attendant, Attendant-in-Ordinary to Grand General Fan, Prince of Le'an, and Administrator of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 還，仍為中書侍郎、本國大中正。

translations.literal: On his return he again served as Gentleman of the Secretariat and Chief Rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he again served as Gentleman of the Secretariat and Chief Rectifier of his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 使酒泉，慰勞沮渠無諱。

translations.literal: He was sent to Jiuquan to console and comfort Juqu Wuhui.
translations.idiomatic: He was dispatched to Jiuquan to console Juqu Wuhui.

sentences.zh: 還，遷散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: On his return he was promoted to Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Gentleman of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 聘劉義隆還，拜給事中、建威將軍，賜爵成臯子。

translations.literal: After an embassy to Liu Yilong he returned and was appointed Palace Attendant and General Who Establishes Might, and granted the title Viscount of Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: After an embassy to Liu Yilong he was appointed Palace Attendant and General Who Establishes Might and enfeoffed as Viscount of Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 出為平東將軍、營州刺史，進爵建安公。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yingzhou, and was advanced to Duke of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served as General Who Pacifies the East and Inspector of Yingzhou and was advanced to Duke of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈征南將軍、并州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was given General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Bingzhou; his posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Bingzhou, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 在州郡以仁德為先，不任刑罰，清身率下，宰守不敢為非。

translations.literal: In prefectures and commanderies he put benevolence and virtue first, did not rely on punishments, kept his person pure to lead those below, and district administrators did not dare do wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In office he put benevolence first, avoided relying on punishments, led by personal example, and local officials did not dare misconduct themselves.

sentences.zh: 子仲慮，太和初，假給事中、高麗副使，尋假散騎常侍、高麗使。

translations.literal: His son Zhonglü, at the beginning of Taihe, was provisionally made Palace Attendant and deputy envoy to Goguryeo; soon after he was provisionally made Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and envoy to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhonglü, at the start of the Taihe era, served provisionally as Palace Attendant and deputy envoy to Goguryeo, then as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry and envoy to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 後出為章武太守，加寧遠將軍。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Administrator of Zhangwu and was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distance.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Administrator of Zhangwu with the additional title General Who Pacifies the Distance.

sentences.zh: 仲慮弟仲繼，學尚有父風，善倉、雅、林說。

translations.literal: Zhonglü's younger brother Zhongji, in learning still bore his father's manner; he was skilled in the Shangshu cang, Shijing ya, and Lin shuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhonglü's younger brother Zhongji preserved his father's scholarly manner and was skilled in the Cang, Ya, and Lin commentaries.

sentences.zh: 太和中，官至侍御長，坐事徙西裔，道死。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he reached the office of Chief of Palace Attendants; for an offense he was banished to the western marches and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era he rose to Chief of Palace Attendants; convicted of an offense, he was banished to the western frontier and died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 梁祚，北地泥陽人。

translations.literal: Liang Zuo was a man of Niyang in Beidi.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zuo was a native of Niyang in Beidi.

sentences.zh: 父劭，皇始二年歸國，拜吏部郎，出為濟陽太守。

translations.literal: His father Shao, in the second year of Huangshi, submitted to the state, was appointed Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, and went out as Administrator of Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shao submitted to the Wei in the second year of Huangshi, was appointed Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, and later served as Administrator of Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 至祚居趙郡。

translations.literal: By the time of Zuo the family resided in Zhao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By Zuo's time the family had settled in Zhao commandery.

sentences.zh: 祚篤志好學，歷治諸經，尤善公羊春秋、鄭氏易，常以教授。

translations.literal: Zuo was devoted in will and loved learning; he studied all the classics in turn and was especially skilled in the Gongyang Spring and Autumn and Zheng's Changes, which he constantly used in instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo was devoted to learning, studied all the classics in turn, and was especially skilled in the Gongyang Commentary and Zheng Xuan's Changes, which he taught throughout his life.

sentences.zh: 有儒者風，而無當世之才。

translations.literal: He had the air of a Confucian scholar but lacked talent for his own age.
translations.idiomatic: He had the bearing of a Confucian scholar but lacked talent for practical affairs of his time.

sentences.zh: 與幽州別駕平恒有舊，又姊先適范陽李氏，遂攜家人僑居於薊。

translations.literal: He had an old friendship with Ping Heng, Vice-Prefect of Youzhou; moreover his elder sister had earlier married into the Li clan of Fanyang, and so he took his family to live as sojourners in Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He was an old friend of Ping Heng, Vice-Prefect of Youzhou, and his elder sister had earlier married into the Li clan of Fanyang; he therefore moved his family to live as sojourners in Ji.

sentences.zh: 積十餘年，雖覊旅貧窘而著述不倦。

translations.literal: For more than ten years, though a sojourner in poverty and want, he never wearied of writing.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years, though living abroad in poverty, he never wearied of writing.

sentences.zh: 恒時相請屈，與論經史。

translations.literal: Heng often invited him to come and discuss the classics and histories together.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Heng often invited him to visit and discuss the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 辟祕書中散，稍遷祕書令。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Secretariat Attendant and gradually promoted to Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Secretariat Attendant and gradually promoted to Secretariat Director.

sentences.zh: 為李訢所排，擯退為中書博士。

translations.literal: He was ostracized by Li Xin and demoted to Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ostracized by Li Xin, he was demoted to Doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 後出為統萬鎮司馬，徵為散令。

translations.literal: Later he went out as Military Administrator of Tongwan garrison and was recalled as Scattered Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Military Administrator of the Tongwan garrison and was recalled as Scattered Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 撰并陳壽三國志，名曰國統。

translations.literal: He compiled and joined Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms, entitling it National Succession.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled a unified edition of Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms, entitled National Succession.

sentences.zh: 又作代都賦，頗行於世。

translations.literal: He also composed the Rhapsody on the Capital of Dai, which circulated considerably in his day.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote the Rhapsody on the Capital of Dai, which circulated widely in his day.

sentences.zh: 清貧守素，不交勢貴。

translations.literal: Pure and poor, he kept to simplicity and did not associate with the powerful and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Poor but upright, he kept to simplicity and did not associate with the powerful.

sentences.zh: 年八十七，太和十二年卒。

translations.literal: At the age of eighty-seven he died in the twelfth year of Taihe.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of Taihe at the age of eighty-seven.

sentences.zh: 子元吉，有父風。

translations.literal: His son Yuanji bore his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanji preserved his father's scholarly manner.

sentences.zh: 少子重，歷碎職，後為相州鎮北府參軍事。

translations.literal: His youngest son Chong passed through minor posts and later became Military Adjutant of the Northern Garrison Headquarters of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His youngest son Chong held various minor posts and later served as Military Adjutant of the Northern Garrison Headquarters of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 平恒，字繼叔，燕國薊人。

translations.literal: Ping Heng, styled Jishu, was a man of Ji in the State of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Ping Heng, courtesy name Jishu, was a native of Ji in Yan.

sentences.zh: 祖視，父儒，並仕慕容為通宦。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shi and father Ru both served Murong as general officials.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shi and father Ru both served the Murong as general officials.

sentences.zh: 恒耽勤讀誦，研綜經籍，鉤深致遠，多所博聞。

translations.literal: Heng was devoted to diligent reading and recitation, researched and synthesized the classics, plumbed the deep to reach the far, and had broad learning in many matters.
translations.idiomatic: Heng devoted himself to reading and recitation, mastered the classics comprehensively, plumbed profound depths, and acquired broad learning.

sentences.zh: 自周以降，暨於魏世，帝王傳代之由，貴臣昇降之緒，皆撰錄品第，商略是非，號曰略注，合百餘篇。

translations.literal: From Zhou downward through the Wei age, the reasons for imperial succession and the threads of noble ministers' rise and fall—he all compiled and ranked them, weighed right and wrong, and called the work Brief Notes, more than a hundred chapters in all.
translations.idiomatic: From the Zhou through the Wei, he compiled and ranked the reasons for dynastic succession and the rises and falls of eminent ministers, weighing right and wrong in a work entitled Brief Notes of more than a hundred chapters.

sentences.zh: 好事者覽之，咸以為善焉。

translations.literal: Those who delighted in such things who read it all considered it excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Readers who delighted in such matters all praised it highly.

sentences.zh: 安貧樂道，不以屢空改操。

translations.literal: Content with poverty and devoted to the Way, he did not alter his conduct because of repeated destitution.
translations.idiomatic: Content with poverty and devoted to the Way, he never altered his conduct despite repeated want.

sentences.zh: 徵為中書博士。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Doctor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Doctor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 久之，出為幽州別駕。

translations.literal: After a long while he went out as Vice-Prefect of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he served as Vice-Prefect of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 廉貞寡欲，不營資產，衣食至常不足，妻子不免飢寒。

translations.literal: Pure and upright, with few desires, he did not pursue assets; food and clothing were often insufficient, and his wife and children could not escape hunger and cold.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and upright with few desires, he pursued no wealth; his food and clothing were often insufficient, and his wife and children knew hunger and cold.

sentences.zh: 後拜著作佐郎，遷祕書丞。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of Composition and promoted to Secretariat Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed Assistant Gentleman of Composition and promoted to Secretariat Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 時高允為監，河間邢祐、[2]北平陽嘏、河東裴定、廣平程駿、金城趙元順等為著作佐郎，雖才學互有短長，然俱為稱職，並號長者。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Yun was supervisor; Xing You of Hejian, [2] Yang Gu of Beiping, Pei Ding of Hedong, Cheng Jun of Guangping, Zhao Yuanshun of Jincheng, and others were Assistant Gentlemen of Composition. Though in talent and learning each had strengths and weaknesses, all were competent in office and were called the elders.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gao Yun served as supervisor, with Xing You of Hejian, [2] Yang Gu of Beiping, Pei Ding of Hedong, Cheng Jun of Guangping, Zhao Yuanshun of Jincheng, and others as Assistant Gentlemen of Composition. Though their talents varied, all performed their duties well and were known as the elders.

sentences.zh: 允每稱博通經籍無過恒也。

translations.literal: Yun often said that in thorough mastery of the classics none surpassed Heng.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun often said that no one surpassed Heng in mastery of the classics.

sentences.zh: 恒即劉彧將軍王玄謨舅子。

translations.literal: Heng was the nephew by marriage of General Wang Xuemo of Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was the nephew by marriage of Liu Yu's general Wang Xuemo.

sentences.zh: 恒三子，並不率父業，好酒自棄。

translations.literal: Heng's three sons all failed to follow their father's profession, loved wine, and abandoned themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's three sons all failed to follow their father's example, loving wine and ruining themselves.

sentences.zh: 恒常忿其世衰，植杖巡舍側崗而哭，不為營事婚宦，任意官娶，故仕聘濁碎，不得及其門流。

translations.literal: Heng often raged at the decline of his line, planted his staff and walked the hill beside his house weeping, did not arrange marriages and offices for them, and let them marry as they pleased—thus their official matches were coarse and fragmented, unable to match his family's standing.
translations.idiomatic: Heng often grieved at his family's decline, leaning on his staff to weep on the hill beside his house. He arranged no marriages or offices for his sons, letting them marry as they pleased; their matches were unworthy and could not sustain the family's standing.

sentences.zh: 恒婦弟鄧宗慶及外生孫玄明等每以為言。

translations.literal: Heng's wife's younger brother Deng Zongqing and his sister's son Sun Xuanming and others often spoke to him about this.
translations.idiomatic: His wife's younger brother Deng Zongqing and his sister's son Sun Xuanming often urged him about this.

sentences.zh: 恒曰：「此輩會是衰頓，何煩勞我。

translations.literal: Heng said, "These fellows are bound to decline and fail—why should they trouble me?"
translations.idiomatic: Heng said, "These fellows are bound to decline—why should they trouble me?"

sentences.zh: 」乃別構精廬，并置經籍於其中，一奴自給，妻子莫得而往，酒食亦不與同。

translations.literal: Thereupon he built a separate refined lodge, placed the classics within it, and had one slave attend him; his wife and children could not go there, nor did he share food and drink with them.
translations.idiomatic: He then built a separate study lodge, stocked it with classics, and kept only one servant; his wife and children were not permitted to enter, nor did he share meals with them.

sentences.zh: 時有珍美，呼時老東安公刁雍等共飲噉之，家人無得嘗焉。

translations.literal: When there were delicacies he summoned the venerable Duke of Dong'an, Diao Yong, and others to eat and drink with him; the family got none to taste.
translations.idiomatic: When delicacies were available he summoned the venerable Duke of Dong'an, Diao Yong, and others to share them; his family tasted none.

sentences.zh: 太和十年，以恒為祕書令，而恒固請為郡，未授而卒，時年七十六。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taihe, Heng was appointed Secretariat Director, but he firmly requested a commandery post; before appointment he died, at the age of seventy-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Taihe he was appointed Secretariat Director, but firmly requested a commandery post; before the appointment was made he died at seventy-six.

sentences.zh: 贈平東將軍、幽州刺史、都昌侯，諡曰康。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Youzhou, and Marquis of Duchang; his posthumous name was Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as General Who Pacifies the East, Inspector of Youzhou, and Marquis of Duchang, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 子壽昌，太和初，祕書令史。

translations.literal: His son Shouchang, at the beginning of Taihe, was Secretariat Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shouchang served as Secretariat Clerk at the start of the Taihe era.

sentences.zh: 稍遷荊州征虜府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: He was gradually promoted to Recording Secretary of the Pacification of Barbarians Headquarters of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Recording Secretary of the Pacification Headquarters of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳奇，字脩奇，河北人也，自云晉涼州刺史驤之八世孫。

translations.literal: Chen Qi, styled Xiuqi, was a man of Hebei and claimed to be the eighth-generation descendant of Xiang, Jin Inspector of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qi, courtesy name Xiuqi, was a native of Hebei who claimed descent in the eighth generation from Xiang, Jin Inspector of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖刃，仕慕容垂。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ren served Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ren served Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 奇少孤，家貧，而奉母至孝。

translations.literal: Qi was orphaned young; his family was poor, yet he served his mother with utmost filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young and poor, Qi nevertheless served his mother with utmost filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 齠齓聰識，有夙成之美。

translations.literal: In infancy he was clever and perceptive, with the beauty of precocious maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Even in childhood he was clever and perceptive, showing precocious brilliance.

sentences.zh: 性氣剛亮，與俗不羣。

translations.literal: His nature and spirit were firm and bright; he did not flock with the vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was firm and forthright; he kept apart from common society.

sentences.zh: 愛玩經典，博通墳籍，常非馬融、鄭玄解經失旨，志在著述五經。

translations.literal: He loved and delighted in the classics, broadly mastered the ancient texts, often criticized Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan for missing the point in interpreting the classics, and aspired to compose commentaries on the Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the classics and mastered the ancient texts, often criticizing Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan for misinterpreting them, and aspired to write commentaries on the Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 始注孝經、論語，頗傳於世，為搢紳所稱。

translations.literal: He first annotated the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, which circulated considerably in his day and were praised by the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: He first annotated the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, which circulated widely and won praise from the gentry.

sentences.zh: 與河間邢祐同召赴京。

translations.literal: Together with Xing You of Hejian he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital together with Xing You of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 時祕書監游雅素聞其名，始頗好之，引入祕省，欲授以史職。

translations.literal: At the time Secretariat Director You Ya had long heard his name, at first favored him considerably, brought him into the Secretariat, and wished to assign him historical duties.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director You Ya had long heard of his reputation, initially favored him, brought him into the Secretariat, and wished to assign him historical duties.

sentences.zh: 後與奇論典誥及詩書，雅贊扶馬鄭。

translations.literal: Later, debating with Qi on the canonical edicts and the Odes and Documents, Ya praised and upheld Ma and Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later, debating with Qi on the canonical edicts and the Odes and Documents, Ya upheld Ma Rong and Zheng Xuan.

sentences.zh: 至於易訟卦天與水違行，雅曰：「自葱嶺以西，水皆西流，推此而言，易之所及自葱嶺以東耳。

translations.literal: Regarding the Song hexagram in the Changes—Heaven and Water moving contrary to each other—Ya said, "West of the Cong Mountains all waters flow westward; by this reasoning, what the Changes covers is only east of the Cong Mountains."
translations.idiomatic: On the Song hexagram—Heaven and Water moving contrary to each other—Ya said, "West of the Cong Mountains all rivers flow westward; by this reasoning, the Changes applies only east of the Cong Mountains."

sentences.zh: 」奇曰：「易理綿廣，包含宇宙。

translations.literal: Qi said, "The principles of the Changes are vast and far-reaching, embracing the cosmos."
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied, "The principles of the Changes are vast and embrace the entire cosmos."

sentences.zh: 若如公言，自葱嶺以西，豈東向望天哉？

translations.literal: If it were as you say, west of the Cong Mountains would people not face east to look at Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: If that were so, would people west of the Cong Mountains not still face east to behold Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 」奇執義非雅，每如此類，終不苟從。

translations.literal: Qi held to principle against Ya; on every matter of this kind he never casually yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Qi held to principle against Ya; on such matters he never yielded casually.

sentences.zh: 雅性護短，因以為嫌。

translations.literal: Ya by nature shielded his own shortcomings and therefore took offense.
translations.idiomatic: Ya was defensive of his own faults and therefore came to resent him.

sentences.zh: 嘗眾辱奇，或爾汝之，或指為小人。

translations.literal: He once humiliated Qi before a crowd, sometimes addressing him with familiar pronouns, sometimes calling him a petty man.
translations.idiomatic: He once humiliated Qi in public, addressing him familiarly or calling him a petty man.

sentences.zh: 奇曰：「公身為君子，奇身且小人耳。

translations.literal: Qi said, "Your person is that of a gentleman; my person is merely that of a petty man."
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied, "You are a gentleman; I am merely a petty man."

sentences.zh: 」雅曰：「君言身且小人，君祖父是何人也？

translations.literal: Ya said, "You say your person is a petty man—what sort of men were your grandfather and father?"
translations.idiomatic: Ya said, "You call yourself a petty man—what sort of men were your grandfather and father?"

sentences.zh: 」奇曰：「祖，燕東部侯釐。

translations.literal: Qi said, "My grandfather was Xi, Marquis of the Eastern Division of Yan."
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied, "My grandfather was Xi, Marquis of the Eastern Division of Yan."

sentences.zh: 」[3]雅質奇曰：「侯釐何官也？

translations.literal: Ya pressed Qi: "What office was Marquis Xi?"
translations.idiomatic: [3] Ya pressed him: "What office did Marquis Xi hold?"

sentences.zh: 」奇曰：「三皇不傳禮，官名豈同哉？

translations.literal: Qi said, "The Three Sovereigns did not transmit ritual; how could office titles be the same?"
translations.idiomatic: Qi replied, "The Three Sovereigns did not transmit ritual—how could office titles remain the same?"

sentences.zh: 故昔有雲師、火正、鳥師之名。

translations.literal: Hence in antiquity there were the titles Cloud Master, Fire Rectifier, and Bird Master.
translations.idiomatic: Hence antiquity knew titles such as Cloud Master, Fire Rectifier, and Bird Master.

sentences.zh: 以斯而言，世革則官異，時易則禮變。

translations.literal: By this reasoning, when the age changes, offices differ; when the times shift, ritual transforms.
translations.idiomatic: By this reasoning, when ages change offices differ, and when times shift ritual transforms.

sentences.zh: 公為皇魏東宮內侍長，侍長竟何職也？

translations.literal: You served as Chief Palace Attendant of the Eastern Palace of Great Wei—what office is Chief Attendant after all?"
translations.idiomatic: You served as Chief Palace Attendant of the Eastern Palace of Great Wei—what office is that, after all?"

sentences.zh: 」由是雅深憾之。

translations.literal: From this Ya bore deep resentment toward him.
translations.idiomatic: From this Ya bore deep resentment toward him.

sentences.zh: 先是敕以奇付雅，令銓補祕書，雅既惡之，遂不復敍用焉。

translations.literal: Earlier an edict had placed Qi under Ya's charge to assess and appoint him to the Secretariat; since Ya detested him, he never again arranged his employment.
translations.idiomatic: An earlier edict had placed Qi under Ya to assess him for Secretariat appointment; since Ya detested him, he never arranged his appointment.

sentences.zh: 奇冗散數年，高允與奇讎溫古籍，嘉其遠致，稱奇通識，非凡學所窺。

translations.literal: Qi was idle and dispersed for several years; Gao Yun, warming ancient texts with Qi in friendly study, praised his far-reaching insight and called Qi comprehensively learned—not what ordinary scholarship could glimpse.
translations.idiomatic: Qi remained idle for several years. Gao Yun studied ancient texts with him, praised his far-reaching insight, and declared his learning beyond ordinary scholarship.

sentences.zh: 允微勸雅曰：「君朝望具瞻，何為與野儒辨簡牘章句？

translations.literal: Yun gently urged Ya, saying, "Your court prestige is universally watched—why debate bamboo slips and chapter-and-phrase minutiae with a rustic scholar?"
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun gently urged Ya, "Your prestige at court is universally watched—why debate textual minutiae with a rustic scholar?"

sentences.zh: 」雅謂允有私於奇，曰：「君寧黨小人也！

translations.literal: Ya thought Yun was partial to Qi and said, "Are you not siding with a petty man!"
translations.idiomatic: Ya thought Yun favored Qi and said, "Are you not siding with a petty man!"

sentences.zh: 」乃取奇所注論語、孝經焚於坑內。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took Qi's annotated Analects and Classic of Filial Piety and burned them in a pit.
translations.idiomatic: He then took Qi's annotated Analects and Classic of Filial Piety and burned them in a pit.

sentences.zh: 奇曰：「公貴人，不乏樵薪，何乃燃奇論語？

translations.literal: Qi said, "You are a noble man—not lacking firewood—why burn Qi's Analects?"
translations.idiomatic: Qi said, "You are a nobleman with no lack of firewood—why burn my Analects?"

sentences.zh: 」雅愈怒，因告京師後生不聽傳授。

translations.literal: Ya grew angrier still and therefore told the young scholars of the capital not to transmit his teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Ya grew angrier still and forbade the young scholars of the capital to study under him.

sentences.zh: 而奇無降志，亦評雅之失。

translations.literal: Yet Qi did not lower his resolve and also criticized Ya's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Qi did not lower his resolve and continued to criticize Ya's faults.

sentences.zh: 雅製昭皇太后碑文，論后名字之美，比諭前魏之甄后。

translations.literal: Ya composed the epitaph for Empress Dowager Zhao, discussing the beauty of the empress's name and comparing her to Empress Zhen of Former Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Ya composed the epitaph for Empress Dowager Zhao, praising the beauty of her name and comparing her to Empress Zhen of Former Wei.

sentences.zh: 奇刺發其非，遂聞於上。

translations.literal: Qi exposed the error, and it reached the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Qi exposed the error, and the matter reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔下司徒檢對碑史事，乃郭后，雅有屈焉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Minister of Works to check the historical facts of the epitaph; it was Empress Guo, and Ya was put in the wrong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the Minister of Works to verify the historical facts; the empress was in fact Empress Guo, and Ya was proven wrong.

sentences.zh: 有人為謗書，多怨時之言，頗稱奇不得志。

translations.literal: Someone composed a slanderous book with many complaints against the times, which spoke considerably of Qi's frustrated ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: Someone composed a slanderous book full of complaints against the times that spoke of Qi's frustrated ambitions.

sentences.zh: 雅乃諷在事云：「此書言奇不遂，當是奇假人為之。

translations.literal: Ya then insinuated to those in office, saying, "This book says Qi did not succeed—Qi must have had someone compose it for him."
translations.idiomatic: Ya then insinuated to officials, "This book speaks of Qi's failure—Qi must have had someone write it for him."

sentences.zh: 如依律文，造謗書者皆及孥戮。

translations.literal: According to the statutes, those who compose slanderous books are punished extending to wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Under the law, those who compose slanderous books are punished together with their families.

sentences.zh: 」遂抵奇罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon charges were laid against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Charges were then laid against Qi.

sentences.zh: 時司徒、平原王陸麗知奇見枉，惜其才學，故得遷延經年，冀有寬宥。

translations.literal: At the time the Minister of Works, Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li, knew Qi was wronged and valued his talent and learning, and therefore the case was delayed for years in hope of pardon.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works, Prince of Pingyuan Lu Li, knew Qi was wronged and valued his talent, delaying the case for years in hope of pardon.

sentences.zh: 但執以獄成，竟致大戮，遂及其家。

translations.literal: But once the case was fixed in prison it ended in execution, and his family was implicated as well.
translations.idiomatic: But once the case was concluded in prison, he was executed and his family implicated as well.

sentences.zh: 奇於易尤長，在獄嘗自筮卦，未及成，乃擥破而歎曰：「吾不度來年冬季！

translations.literal: Qi was especially skilled in the Changes; in prison he once divined for himself, and before completion he gathered up and broke the stalks, sighing, "I do not expect to pass the coming winter!"
translations.idiomatic: Qi was especially skilled in the Changes; in prison he once divined for himself, but before completing the hexagram he broke the stalks and sighed, "I do not expect to survive the coming winter!"

sentences.zh: 」及奇受害，如其所占。

translations.literal: When Qi met his fate, it was as he had divined.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was executed, events unfolded exactly as he had divined.

sentences.zh: 奇初被召，夜夢星墜壓脚，明而告人曰：「星則好風，星則好雨，夢星壓脚，必無善徵。

translations.literal: When Qi was first summoned, he dreamed at night that a star fell and pressed his foot; at dawn he told others, "Stars mean fine wind; stars mean good rain—a dream of a star pressing the foot surely has no auspicious sign."
translations.idiomatic: When Qi was first summoned, he dreamed that a star fell upon his foot. At dawn he told others, "Stars presage wind and rain—a star falling on one's foot can hardly be auspicious."

sentences.zh: 但時命峻切，不敢不赴耳。

translations.literal: But the times' mandate was stern and urgent—I dared not fail to go."
translations.idiomatic: But the summons was urgent—I dared not refuse."

sentences.zh: 」奇妹適常氏，有子曰矯之，仕歷郡守。

translations.literal: Qi's younger sister married into the Chang clan and had a son Jiaozhi, who served through the ranks to commandery administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's younger sister married into the Chang clan; her son Jiaozhi rose to serve as commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 神龜中，上書陳時政所宜，言頗忠至，清河王懌稱美之。

translations.literal: In the Shengui era he submitted a memorial setting forth what was fitting in current policy; his words were quite loyal and sincere, and Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi praised him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shengui era he submitted a memorial on current policy that was notably loyal and sincere; Prince of Qinghe Yuan Yi praised it.

sentences.zh: 奇所注論語，矯之傳掌，未能行於世，其義多異鄭玄，往往與司徒崔浩同。

translations.literal: Qi's annotated Analects was transmitted and held by Jiaozhi but could not circulate in the world; its meanings often differed from Zheng Xuan and frequently agreed with Minister of Works Cui Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's annotated Analects was preserved by Jiaozhi but never circulated widely; its interpretations often differed from Zheng Xuan and frequently agreed with Minister of Works Cui Hao.

sentences.zh: 常爽，字仕明，河內溫人，魏太常卿林六世孫也。

translations.literal: Chang Shuang, styled Shiming, was a man of Wen in Henei, sixth-generation descendant of Lin, Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shuang, courtesy name Shiming, was a native of Wen in Henei and sixth-generation descendant of Lin, Wei Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 祖珍，苻堅南安太守，因世亂遂居涼州。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhen was Administrator of Nan'an under Fu Jian; because of the age's turmoil he then resided in Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhen served as Administrator of Nan'an under Fu Jian and settled in Liangzhou during the turmoil of the age.

sentences.zh: 父坦，乞伏世鎮遠將軍、大夏鎮將、顯美侯。

translations.literal: His father Tan was General Who Pacifies the Distance, Garrison Commander of Daxia, and Marquis of Xianmei under the Qifu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan served the Qifu as General Who Pacifies the Distance, Garrison Commander of Daxia, and Marquis of Xianmei.

sentences.zh: 爽少而聰敏，嚴正有志概，雖家人僮隸未嘗見其寬誕之容。

translations.literal: Shuang from youth was clever and keen, stern and upright with aspiring spirit; even family servants and slaves never saw him with a lax or unrestrained countenance.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shuang was clever and keen, stern and upright; even family servants never saw him with a lax or unrestrained manner.

sentences.zh: 篤志好學，博聞強識，明習緯候，五經百家多所研綜。

translations.literal: Devoted in will and loving learning, broadly informed with strong memory, clearly versed in prognostic texts, he researched and synthesized much among the Five Classics and the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to learning, broadly informed with a strong memory, versed in prognostic texts, he mastered the Five Classics and the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 州郡禮命皆不就。

translations.literal: Courteous summons from prefectures and commanderies he never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined all courteous summons from prefectures and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 世祖西征涼土，爽與兄仕國歸款軍門，世祖嘉之。

translations.literal: When Shizu campaigned west against the Liang region, Shuang and his elder brother Shiguo submitted in good faith at the army gate; Shizu commended them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taiwu campaigned west against Liang, Shuang and his elder brother Shiguo submitted at the army gate, and the emperor commended them.

sentences.zh: 賜仕國爵五品，顯美男；

translations.literal: Shiguo was granted a fifth-rank title, Baron of Xiannan;
translations.idiomatic: Shiguo was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Baron of Xiannan;

sentences.zh: 爽為六品，拜宣威將軍。

translations.literal: Shuang was sixth rank and appointed General Who Proclaims Might.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang received sixth rank and was appointed General Who Proclaims Might.

sentences.zh: 是時戎車屢駕，征伐為事，貴遊子弟未遑學術，爽置館溫水之右，教授門徒七百餘人，京師學業，翕然復興。

translations.literal: At that time war chariots were repeatedly deployed and campaigns were the business of the day; sons of the noble and roaming had no leisure for learning. Shuang established a hall on the right bank of the Wen River and instructed more than seven hundred disciples; learning in the capital flourished anew as one.
translations.idiomatic: War chariots were constantly deployed and campaigns the order of the day; sons of the nobility had no leisure for study. Shuang established a school on the right bank of the Wen River and instructed more than seven hundred disciples, and learning in the capital flourished anew.

sentences.zh: 爽立訓甚有勸罰之科，弟子事之若嚴君焉。

translations.literal: Shuang established instruction with strict rules of reward and punishment; disciples served him as they would a stern lord.
translations.idiomatic: Shuang established strict rules of reward and punishment; his disciples served him as they would a stern master.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射元贊、平原太守司馬真安、著作郎程靈虬，皆是爽教所就。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat Yuan Zan, Administrator of Pingyuan Sima Zhen'an, and Gentleman of Composition Cheng Lingqiu were all products of Shuang's teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister Yuan Zan, Administrator of Pingyuan Sima Zhen'an, and Gentleman of Composition Cheng Lingqiu were all products of Shuang's teaching.

sentences.zh: 崔浩、高允並稱爽之嚴教，奬厲有方。

translations.literal: Cui Hao and Gao Yun both praised Shuang's stern instruction and his well-directed encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao and Gao Yun both praised Shuang's stern instruction and well-directed encouragement.

sentences.zh: 允曰：「文翁柔勝，先生剛克，立教雖殊，成人一也。

translations.literal: Yun said, "Wen Weng overcame through gentleness; the Master overcomes through firmness—though the teaching established differs, making adults of men is one."
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yun said, "Wen Weng overcame through gentleness; the Master through firmness—though their methods differed, both shaped worthy men."

sentences.zh: 」其為通識歎服如此。

translations.literal: Such was the comprehensive understanding with which he was admired and submitted to.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the comprehensive understanding with which men admired him.

sentences.zh: 因教授之暇，述六經略注，以廣制作，甚有條貫。

translations.literal: In the intervals of instruction he composed Brief Commentaries on the Six Classics to extend the work of creation, with excellent systematic order.
translations.idiomatic: In intervals between teaching he composed Brief Commentaries on the Six Classics to extend the canonical tradition, arranged with excellent systematic order.

sentences.zh: 其序曰：「傳稱：『立天之道曰陰與陽，立地之道曰柔與剛，立人之道曰仁與義。

translations.literal: Its preface says: "The tradition states: 'Establishing Heaven's Way is called yin and yang; establishing Earth's Way is called soft and hard; establishing Man's Way is called benevolence and righteousness.'"
translations.idiomatic: Its preface reads: "The tradition states: 'Establishing Heaven's Way means yin and yang; establishing Earth's Way means soft and hard; establishing Man's Way means benevolence and righteousness.'"

sentences.zh: 』然則仁義者人之性也，經典者身之文也，皆以陶鑄神情，啟悟耳目，未有不由學而能成其器，不由習而能利其業。

translations.literal: Thus benevolence and righteousness are man's nature, and the classics are the ornament of the person—both serve to mold spirit and feeling and open the ears and eyes. Never has anyone, without learning, been able to complete his vessel, or without practice been able to profit his work.
translations.idiomatic: Thus benevolence and righteousness are human nature, and the classics are the ornament of the person—both mold spirit and enlighten the mind. No one has ever perfected his character without learning, or mastered his craft without practice.

sentences.zh: 是故季路勇士也，服道以成忠烈之概；

translations.literal: Therefore Zilu was a brave warrior, yet by submitting to the Way he achieved the stature of loyal valor;
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zilu was a brave warrior, yet by submitting to the Way he achieved loyal valor;

sentences.zh: 甯越庸夫也，講藝以全高尚之節。

translations.literal: Ning Yue was a common fellow, yet by studying the arts he preserved exalted integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Yue was a common fellow, yet by studying the arts he preserved exalted integrity.

sentences.zh: 蓋所由者習也，所因者本也，本立而道生，身文而德備焉。

translations.literal: What one follows is practice; what one relies on is the root. When the root is established the Way is born; when the person is ornamented, virtue is complete.
translations.idiomatic: What one follows is practice; what one relies on is the root. When the root is established the Way arises; when the person is cultivated, virtue is complete.

sentences.zh: 昔者先王之訓天下也，莫不導以詩書，教以禮樂，移其風俗，和其人民。

translations.literal: Of old when the former kings instructed the realm, none failed to guide it with the Odes and Documents, teach it with ritual and music, transform its customs, and harmonize its people.
translations.idiomatic: Of old the former kings instructed the realm by guiding it with the Odes and Documents, teaching it with ritual and music, transforming its customs, and harmonizing its people.

sentences.zh: 故恭儉莊敬而不煩者，教深於禮也；

translations.literal: Thus those who are reverent, frugal, dignified, and respectful without being troubled—their teaching is deep in ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Thus those who are reverent, frugal, dignified, and respectful without vexation have been deeply taught by ritual;

sentences.zh: 廣博易良而不奢者，教深於樂也；

translations.literal: those who are broad, easy, and good without being extravagant—their teaching is deep in music;
translations.idiomatic: those who are broad-minded, easy, and good without extravagance have been deeply taught by music;

sentences.zh: 溫柔敦厚而不愚者，教深於詩也；

translations.literal: those who are gentle, soft, and sincere without being foolish—their teaching is deep in the Odes;
translations.idiomatic: those who are gentle, soft, and sincere without foolishness have been deeply taught by the Odes;

sentences.zh: 疏通知遠而不誣者，教深於書也；

translations.literal: those who are penetrating, intelligent, and far-seeing without being deceptive—their teaching is deep in the Documents;
translations.idiomatic: those who are penetrating, intelligent, and far-seeing without deception have been deeply taught by the Documents;

sentences.zh: 潔靜精微而不賊者，教深於易也；

translations.literal: those who are pure, tranquil, subtle, and refined without being harmful—their teaching is deep in the Changes;
translations.idiomatic: those who are pure, tranquil, subtle, and refined without harm have been deeply taught by the Changes;

sentences.zh: 屬辭比事而不亂者，教深於春秋也。

translations.literal: those who arrange words and compare events without disorder—their teaching is deep in the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: those who arrange words and compare events without disorder have been deeply taught by the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 夫樂以和神，詩以正言，禮以明體，書以廣聽，春秋以斷事，五者蓋五常之道相須而備，而易為之源。

translations.literal: Now music harmonizes the spirit, the Odes rectify speech, ritual clarifies form, the Documents broaden hearing, and the Spring and Autumn adjudicate affairs—these five are the Way of the five constants, mutually needed and complete, with the Changes as their source.
translations.idiomatic: Music harmonizes the spirit; the Odes rectify speech; ritual clarifies form; the Documents broaden understanding; the Spring and Autumn adjudicate affairs. These five embody the Way of the five constants, mutually sustaining one another—and the Changes are their source.

sentences.zh: 故曰：「易不可見則乾坤其幾乎息矣。

translations.literal: Thus it is said: "If the Changes cannot be perceived, then Heaven and Earth would nearly cease!"
translations.idiomatic: Thus it is said: "If the Changes cannot be seen, Heaven and Earth would almost come to rest."

sentences.zh: 」由是言之，六經者先王之遺烈，聖人之盛事也。

translations.literal: " From this perspective, the Six Classics are the surviving glory of the former kings, the splendid achievement of the sages.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that the Six Classics are the enduring legacy of the former kings and the supreme accomplishment of the sages.

sentences.zh: 安可不遊心寓目，習性文身哉！

translations.literal: How could one fail to fix the mind and lodge the eyes therein, cultivate one's nature and ornament one's person!
translations.idiomatic: How could one fail to give one's heart and attention to them, cultivate one's nature, and adorn one's person through them!

sentences.zh: 頃因暇日，屬意藝林，略撰所聞，討論其本，名曰六經略注以訓門徒焉。

translations.literal: Recently, on a day of leisure, I turned my attention to the grove of arts, briefly compiled what I have heard, examined their roots, and named it Brief Commentaries on the Six Classics to instruct my disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, on a day of leisure, I turned my attention to the forest of learning, briefly set down what I have heard, examined their foundations, and named the work Brief Commentaries on the Six Classics to instruct my disciples.

sentences.zh: 」其略注行於世。

translations.literal: " His brief commentaries circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His Brief Commentaries circulated in the world.

sentences.zh: 爽不事王侯，獨守閑靜，講肄經典二十餘年，時人號為「儒林先生」。

translations.literal: Shuang did not serve kings and marquises; he alone kept to quiet seclusion, lecturing and studying the classics for more than twenty years, and men of the age called him "Master Lin of the Confucians."
translations.idiomatic: Shuang did not serve kings or marquises. He lived alone in quiet seclusion, lecturing and studying the classics for more than twenty years, and men of the age called him "Master Lin of the Confucians."

sentences.zh: 年六十三，卒於家。

translations.literal: At age sixty-three he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 子文通，歷官至鎮西司馬、南天水太守、西翼校尉。

translations.literal: His son Wentong rose through the ranks to General Who Pacifies the West, Administrator of Southern Tianshui, and Colonel of the Western Wing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wentong rose through the ranks to serve as General Who Pacifies the West, Administrator of Southern Tianshui, and Colonel of the Western Wing.

sentences.zh: 文通子景，別有傳。

translations.literal: Wentong's son Jing has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Wentong's son Jing has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 劉獻之，博陵饒陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Xianzhi was a man of Raoyang in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xianzhi was a native of Raoyang in Boling.

sentences.zh: 少而孤貧，雅好詩、傳，曾受業於勃海程玄，後遂博觀眾籍。

translations.literal: From youth he was orphaned and poor; he naturally loved the Odes and the Commentary, once studied under Cheng Xuan of Bohai, and afterward broadly viewed many texts.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor from youth, he naturally loved the Odes and the Commentary. He once studied under Cheng Xuan of Bohai and afterward read widely among many texts.

sentences.zh: 見名法之言，掩卷而笑曰：「若使楊墨之流不為此書，千載誰知其小也！

translations.literal: When he saw writings on Legalism, he would close the scroll and laugh, saying, "If Yang and Mo and their kind had not written this book, who after a thousand years would know how petty they are!"
translations.idiomatic: When he encountered Legalist writings, he would close the scroll and laugh, saying, "If Yang Zhu, Mozi, and their followers had not written this book, who after a thousand years would know how small-minded they were!"

sentences.zh: 」曾謂其所親曰：「觀屈原離騷之作，自是狂人，死其宜矣，何足惜也！

translations.literal: " Once he told those close to him, "Reading Qu Yuan's Li Sao, he was plainly a madman; his death was fitting—what is there to regret!"
translations.idiomatic: Once he told those close to him, "Reading Qu Yuan's Li Sao, one sees plainly a madman. His death was fitting—what is there to regret!"

sentences.zh: 吾常謂濯纓洗耳，有異人之迹；

translations.literal: I often say that washing the cap-strings and washing the ears show the traces of extraordinary men;
translations.idiomatic: I often say that washing one's cap-strings and washing one's ears show the marks of extraordinary men;

sentences.zh: 哺糟歠醨，有同物之志。

translations.literal: sucking lees and drinking dregs show the mind of one who is the same as the thing.
translations.idiomatic: while sucking lees and drinking dregs shows the mind of one who has become one with what he consumes.

sentences.zh: 而孔子曰：『我則異於是，無可無不可。

translations.literal: Yet Confucius said, 'I on my part am different from this—there is nothing I must do, and nothing I must not do.'
translations.idiomatic: Yet Confucius said, 'I for my part am not like this—there is nothing I insist on, and nothing I insist against.'

sentences.zh: 』誠哉斯言，實獲我心。」

translations.literal: ' Truly that saying—it truly speaks to my heart."
translations.idiomatic: Truly that saying—it speaks directly to my heart."

sentences.zh: 時人有從獻之學者，獻之輒謂之曰：「人之立身，雖百行殊途，準之四科，要以德行為首。

translations.literal: When men came to study under Xianzhi, he always told them, "In establishing oneself, though the hundred practices have different paths, measured against the four categories, conduct and virtue must come first.
translations.idiomatic: When men came to study under Xianzhi, he always told them, "In establishing oneself, though the hundred practices follow different paths, measured by the four categories of disciples, conduct and virtue must come first.

sentences.zh: 君若能入孝出悌，忠信仁讓，不待出戶，天下自知。

translations.literal: If you can enter with filial piety and emerge with fraternal duty, loyalty, trustworthiness, benevolence, and forbearance, without waiting to leave your door the world will know of itself.
translations.idiomatic: If you can be filial at home and respectful abroad, loyal, trustworthy, benevolent, and forbearing, the world will know of you without your ever leaving your door.

sentences.zh: 儻不能然，雖復下帷針股，躡屩從師，正可博聞多識，不過為土龍乞雨，眩惑將來，其於立身之道有何益乎？

translations.literal: If you cannot be thus, even if you hang down the curtain, pin your thigh with a needle, and put on straw sandals to follow a teacher, you may only become broadly informed and much knowing—nothing more than a clay dragon used to pray for rain, dazzling those to come—what benefit is that for the Way of establishing oneself?
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot be thus, even if you study behind closed curtains, pin your thigh to stay awake, and wear straw sandals to follow a teacher, you may become broadly informed at best—nothing more than a clay dragon used to pray for rain, dazzling future generations. What good is that for the art of living?

sentences.zh: 孔門之徒，初亦未悟，見臯魚之歎，方歸而養親。

translations.literal: Disciples of Confucius's gate at first also failed to comprehend; upon hearing Gaoyu's lament, they then returned home to nurture their parents.
translations.idiomatic: Even disciples of Confucius's school at first failed to understand; only after hearing Gaoyu's lament did they return home to care for their parents.

sentences.zh: [4]嗟乎先達，何自覺之晚也！

translations.literal: [4] Alas, you advanced ones—why do you awaken only so late!
translations.idiomatic: [4] Alas, you who have gone before—why do you awaken to this only so late!

sentences.zh: 束脩不易，受之亦難，敢布心腹，子其圖之。

translations.literal: The bundle of dried meat is not easily changed; accepting instruction is also hard—I dare lay bare my inmost thoughts; you must consider this.
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial gift of dried meat is not lightly given, nor is instruction easily received. I dare lay bare my inmost thoughts—consider this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」由是四方學者莫不高其行義而希造其門。

translations.literal: " From this, scholars from the four directions all held his conduct and righteousness in high esteem and hoped to reach his gate.
translations.idiomatic: From this, scholars from all directions admired his conduct and righteousness and hoped to study at his gate.

sentences.zh: 獻之善春秋、毛詩，每講左氏，盡隱公八年便止，云義例已了，不復須解。

translations.literal: Xianzhi was skilled in the Spring and Autumn and the Mao Odes; each time he lectured on the Zuo Commentary, he stopped entirely at Duke Yin's eighth year, saying the principles and patterns were complete and no further explanation was needed.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi excelled in the Spring and Autumn and the Mao Odes. Each time he lectured on the Zuo Commentary he stopped at the eighth year of Duke Yin, saying the principles and patterns were complete and needed no further explanation.

sentences.zh: 由是弟子不能究竟其說。

translations.literal: Because of this his disciples could not fully complete his exposition.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this his disciples could never fully master his teaching.

sentences.zh: 後本郡舉孝廉，非其好也，逼遣之，乃應命，至京，稱疾而還。

translations.literal: Later his home commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt; it was not to his liking, but he was pressed and sent forth; he then accepted the commission, reached the capital, claimed illness, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later his home commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt. It was not to his liking, but he was compelled to go. He accepted the summons, reached the capital, pleaded illness, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 高祖幸中山，詔徵典內校書，獻之喟然歎曰：「吾不如莊周散木遠矣！

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen visited Zhongshan, an edict summoned him to direct Palace Inner collation of books. Xianzhi sighed deeply and said, "I am far short of Zhuang Zhou's useless tree!
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen visited Zhongshan, an edict summoned him to direct the collation of books within the palace. Xianzhi sighed deeply and said, "I am far from matching Zhuang Zhou's useless tree!

sentences.zh: 一之謂甚，其可再乎。

translations.literal: To go once is already too much—how could one go a second time?
translations.idiomatic: Once is already too much—how could it happen again?

sentences.zh: 」固以疾辭。

translations.literal: " He firmly declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 時中山張吾貴與獻之齊名，海內皆曰儒宗。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Wugui of Zhongshan was equally famous with Xianzhi; throughout the realm both were called patriarchs of Confucianism.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhang Wugui of Zhongshan was equally renowned with Xianzhi; throughout the empire both were hailed as patriarchs of Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 吾貴每一講唱，門徒千數，其行業可稱者寡。

translations.literal: Each time Wugui lectured, his disciples numbered in the thousands, yet few among them had practice worth naming.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Wugui lectured his disciples numbered in the thousands, yet few among them had conduct or achievement worth praising.

sentences.zh: 獻之著錄，數百而已，皆經通之士。

translations.literal: Xianzhi's registered disciples numbered only in the hundreds, yet all were masters who had penetrated the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhi's registered disciples numbered only in the hundreds, yet all were scholars who had thoroughly mastered the classics.

sentences.zh: 於是有識者辨其優劣。

translations.literal: Thereupon men of discernment distinguished their respective merits.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon men of discernment judged which of the two was superior.

sentences.zh: 魏承喪亂之後，五經大義雖有師說，而海內諸生多有疑滯，咸決於獻之。

translations.literal: Wei inherited the aftermath of ruin and disorder; though the great meaning of the Five Classics had masters' explanations, many students within the seas still had doubts and impediments—all resolved them through Xianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei inherited the aftermath of war and disorder. Though the great meaning of the Five Classics had masters' explanations, many students throughout the empire still harbored doubts—and all resolved them through Xianzhi.

sentences.zh: 六藝之文，雖不悉注，然所標宗旨，頗異舊義，撰三禮大義四卷，三傳略例三卷，注毛詩序義一卷，今行於世，并章句疏三卷。

translations.literal: Though he did not annotate all the texts of the Six Arts, the principles he marked out differed considerably from old interpretations. He compiled Great Meanings of the Three Rites in four juan, Brief Patterns of the Three Commentaries in three juan, and Annotation on the Meaning of the Preface to the Mao Odes in one juan—all now circulating; together with Commentary and Sentence Glosses in three juan.
translations.idiomatic: Though he did not annotate all the texts of the Six Arts, the principles he set forth differed considerably from older interpretations. He compiled Great Meanings of the Three Rites in four juan, Brief Patterns of the Three Commentaries in three juan, and Annotation on the Meaning of the Preface to the Mao Odes in one juan—all still in circulation—together with Commentary and Sentence Glosses in three juan.

sentences.zh: 注湼槃經未就而卒。

translations.literal: He was annotating the Nirvana Sutra but died before completing it.
translations.idiomatic: He was annotating the Nirvana Sutra but died before finishing the work.

sentences.zh: 有四子，放古、爰古、參古、脩古。

translations.literal: He had four sons: Fanggu, Yuangu, Cangu, and Xiugu.
translations.idiomatic: He had four sons: Fanggu, Yuangu, Cangu, and Xiugu.

sentences.zh: 放古，幼有人才。

translations.literal: Fanggu from youth had talent.
translations.idiomatic: Fanggu showed talent from youth.

sentences.zh: 為州從事，早亡。

translations.literal: He served as a commandery aide and died early.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a commandery aide and died young.

sentences.zh: 爰古、參古，並傳父詩而不能精通也。

translations.literal: Yuangu and Cangu both transmitted their father's Odes but could not master them thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Yuangu and Cangu both inherited their father's Odes but could not master them fully.

sentences.zh: 張吾貴，字吳子，中山人。
