translations.literal: Zhang Wugui, styled Wuzi, was a man of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wugui, courtesy name Wuzi, was a native of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 少聰惠口辯，身長八尺，容貌奇偉。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and eloquent, eight feet tall, with an extraordinarily imposing appearance.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was clever and eloquent, eight feet tall, with a striking and imposing appearance.

sentences.zh: 年十八，本郡舉為太學博士。

translations.literal: At eighteen his home commandery recommended him as Imperial University doctoral chair.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen his home commandery recommended him as doctoral chair of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 吾貴先未多學，乃從酈詮受禮，牛天祐受易。

translations.literal: Wugui had not previously studied much; he then received Rites from Li Quan and Changes from Niu Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: Wugui had not studied much at first. He then studied Rites under Li Quan and the Changes under Niu Tianyou.

sentences.zh: 詮、祐粗為開發，而吾貴覽讀一遍，便即別構戶牖。

translations.literal: Quan and You opened the texts only in rough outline, yet Wugui read each through once and at once constructed his own doors and windows.
translations.idiomatic: Quan and You gave him only a rough introduction, yet Wugui read each text through once and at once developed his own independent interpretations.

sentences.zh: 世人競歸之。

translations.literal: Men of the world all rushed to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars everywhere flocked to him.

sentences.zh: 曾在夏學，聚徒千數而不講傳，生徒竊云張生之於左氏似不能說。

translations.literal: He once taught at a summer school, gathering disciples in the thousands yet without lecturing on the Commentary; students whispered among themselves that Master Zhang seemed unable to expound the Zuo Commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He once taught at a summer academy, gathering more than a thousand disciples without ever lecturing on the Commentary. Students whispered among themselves that Master Zhang seemed unable to expound the Zuo Commentary.

sentences.zh: 吾貴聞之，謂其徒曰：「我今夏講暫罷，後當說傳，君等來日皆當持本。

translations.literal: Wugui heard this and told his disciples, "My summer lectures are temporarily suspended; later I will expound the Commentary—you must all bring your texts on the appointed day."
translations.idiomatic: Wugui heard this and told his disciples, "My summer lectures are temporarily suspended. Later I will expound the Commentary—you must all bring your texts on the appointed day."

sentences.zh: 」生徒怪之而已。

translations.literal: " The students found it strange, that was all.
translations.idiomatic: The students found it strange, that was all.

sentences.zh: 吾貴謂劉蘭云：「君曾讀左氏，為我一說。

translations.literal: Wugui said to Liu Lan, "You have read the Zuo Commentary—expound it once for me."
translations.idiomatic: Wugui said to Liu Lan, "You have read the Zuo Commentary—lecture on it for me."

sentences.zh: 」蘭遂為講。

translations.literal: " Lan then lectured.
translations.idiomatic: Lan then lectured.

sentences.zh: 三旬之中，吾貴兼讀杜、服，隱括兩家，異同悉舉。

translations.literal: Within thirty days Wugui read both Du Yu and Fu Qian in full, shaped and condensed the two schools, and set forth all their differences and agreements.
translations.idiomatic: Within thirty days Wugui read both Du Yu and Fu Qian in full, synthesized the two schools, and set forth all their points of agreement and disagreement.

sentences.zh: 諸生後集，便為講之，義例無窮，皆多新異。

translations.literal: When the students gathered afterward, he at once lectured—principles and patterns without end, nearly all of them novel and unusual.
translations.idiomatic: When the students gathered afterward, he lectured at once—principles and patterns without end, nearly all of them novel and unusual.

sentences.zh: 蘭乃伏聽。

translations.literal: Lan then listened humbly.
translations.idiomatic: Lan listened humbly from below.

sentences.zh: 學者以此益奇之。

translations.literal: Scholars on this account admired him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars admired him all the more for this.

sentences.zh: 而以辯能飾非，好為詭說，由是業不久傳，而氣陵牧守，不屈王侯，竟不仕而終。

translations.literal: Yet because he could use debate to cover his faults and loved to spin clever sophistries, his learning did not long endure; overbearing toward prefects and governors, yielding to neither kings nor marquises, he never took office and died in that state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet because he used debate to cover his errors and loved to spin clever sophistries, his learning did not long endure. Overbearing toward prefects and governors, he bowed to neither kings nor marquises, never took office, and died in that state.

sentences.zh: 劉蘭，武邑人。

translations.literal: Liu Lan was a man of Wuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lan was a native of Wuyi.

sentences.zh: 年三十餘，始入小學，書急就篇。

translations.literal: At over thirty he first entered elementary school and wrote out the Rapid Primer.
translations.idiomatic: Not until he was over thirty did he enter elementary school and copy out the Rapid Primer.

sentences.zh: 家人覺其聰敏，遂令從師，受春秋、詩、禮於中山王保安。

translations.literal: His family perceived his keen intelligence and had him follow a teacher, receiving the Spring and Autumn, Odes, and Rites from Wang Bao'an of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: His family saw how clever he was and had him study under a teacher, learning the Spring and Autumn, Odes, and Rites from Wang Bao'an of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 家貧無以自資，且耕且學。

translations.literal: His family was poor and had nothing with which to support him; he both farmed and studied.
translations.idiomatic: His family was too poor to support him, so he farmed and studied at the same time.

sentences.zh: 三年之後，便白其兄：「蘭欲講書。

translations.literal: After three years he told his elder brother, "Lan wishes to lecture on the classics."
translations.idiomatic: After three years he told his elder brother, "Lan wishes to lecture on the classics."

sentences.zh: 」其兄笑而聽之，為立黌舍，聚徒二百。

translations.literal: " His elder brother laughed but assented, built a school hall, and gathered two hundred disciples.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother laughed but agreed, built a school hall, and gathered two hundred disciples.

sentences.zh: 蘭讀左氏，五日一遍，兼通五經。

translations.literal: Lan read the Zuo Commentary one full cycle every five days and mastered all Five Classics.
translations.idiomatic: Lan read through the Zuo Commentary once every five days and mastered all Five Classics.

sentences.zh: 先是張吾貴以聰辨過人，其所解說，不本先儒之旨。

translations.literal: Previously Zhang Wugui's brilliance and eloquence surpassed others, but his explications did not rest on the intent of earlier Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Zhang Wugui's brilliance and eloquence surpassed others, but his explications did not rest on the intent of earlier Confucians.

sentences.zh: 唯蘭推經、傳之由，本注者之意，參以緯候及先儒舊事，甚為精悉。

translations.literal: Only Lan traced the sources of the classics and commentaries, grounded himself in the annotators' intent, consulted prognostic texts and old accounts of earlier Confucians—exceedingly precise and thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Only Lan traced the origins of the classics and commentaries, grounded his work in the annotators' intent, and consulted prognostic texts and old accounts of earlier Confucians—making his scholarship exceedingly precise and thorough.

sentences.zh: 自後經義審博，皆由於蘭。

translations.literal: From then on, the thorough breadth of classic meaning all flowed from Lan.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, the depth and breadth of classical interpretation owed everything to Lan.

sentences.zh: 蘭又明陰陽，博物多識，為儒者所宗。

translations.literal: Lan was also versed in yin and yang, broadly learned and much knowing, and was revered by Confucian scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Lan was also versed in yin and yang, broadly learned and deeply knowledgeable, and was revered by Confucian scholars.

sentences.zh: 瀛州刺史裴植徵蘭講書於州城南館，植為學主，故生徒甚盛，海內稱焉。

translations.literal: Pei Zhi, Inspector of Yingzhou, summoned Lan to lecture at the south hall of the prefecture; Zhi served as master of the school, and so disciples were exceedingly numerous—famed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zhi, Inspector of Yingzhou, summoned Lan to lecture at the south hall of the prefecture. Zhi served as master of the school, and disciples were exceedingly numerous—Lan was famed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 又特為中山王英所重。

translations.literal: He was also especially valued by Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He was also especially valued by Prince of Zhongshan Yuan Ying.

sentences.zh: 英引在館，令授其子熙、誘、略等。

translations.literal: Ying brought him into his residence and had him instruct his sons Xi, You, Lue, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Ying brought him into his residence and had him instruct his sons Xi, You, Lue, and the others.

sentences.zh: 蘭學徒前後數千，成業者眾，而排毀公羊，又非董仲舒，由是見譏於世。

translations.literal: Lan's disciples over time numbered in the thousands and many completed their training, yet because he rejected and slandered the Gongyang Commentary and also criticized Dong Zhongshu, he was thereby mocked by the world.
translations.idiomatic: Lan's disciples over the years numbered in the thousands and many completed their training, yet because he rejected and denounced the Gongyang Commentary and also criticized Dong Zhongshu, he was mocked by the world.

sentences.zh: 永平中，為國子助教。

translations.literal: During Yongping he served as Assistant Instructor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongping era he served as Assistant Instructor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，靜坐讀書，有人叩門，門人通焉，蘭命引入。

translations.literal: During Yanqu he was reading quietly when someone knocked at the door; a disciple announced the visitor, and Lan ordered him brought in.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanqu era he was reading quietly when someone knocked at the door. A disciple announced the visitor, and Lan ordered him admitted.

sentences.zh: 其人葛巾單衣，入與蘭坐，謂蘭曰：「君自是學士，何為每見毀辱，理義長短，竟知在誰，而過無禮見陵也。

translations.literal: The man wore a hemp headcloth and simple clothes; entering, he sat with Lan and said, "You are a scholar—why do you suffer insult after insult? Whether doctrine and principle are right or wrong, who ultimately knows? Yet you are rudely overcome without courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: The man wore a hemp headcloth and simple clothes. Entering, he sat with Lan and said, "You are a scholar—why do you suffer insult after insult? Whether doctrine and principle are right or wrong, who can ultimately say? Yet you are overcome rudely and without courtesy.

sentences.zh: 今欲相召，當與君正之。

translations.literal: Now I wish to summon you—we shall set this right with you."
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to summon you—we shall settle this with you."

sentences.zh: 」言終而出。

translations.literal: " Having finished speaking he went out.
translations.idiomatic: Having finished speaking, he went out.

sentences.zh: 出後，蘭告家人。

translations.literal: After he left, Lan told his family.
translations.idiomatic: After the visitor left, Lan told his family what had happened.

sentences.zh: 少時而患卒。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was stricken and died suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was stricken and died suddenly.

sentences.zh: 孫惠蔚，字叔炳，武邑武遂人也，小字陀羅。

translations.literal: Sun Huiwei, styled Shubing, was a native of Wusui in Wuyi; his childhood name was Tuoluo.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huiwei, courtesy name Shubing, was a native of Wusui in Wuyi; his childhood name was Tuoluo.

sentences.zh: 自言六世祖道恭為晉長秋卿，自道恭至惠蔚世以儒學相傳。

translations.literal: He said his sixth-generation ancestor Dao Gong was Jin Director of the Palace Parks; from Dao Gong to Huiwei the family transmitted Confucian learning generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: He said his sixth-generation ancestor Dao Gong had been Jin Director of the Palace Parks, and from Dao Gong down to Huiwei the family had transmitted Confucian learning from generation to generation.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚年十三，粗通詩、書及孝經、論語；

translations.literal: At thirteen Huiwei had a rough mastery of the Odes, Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects;
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen Huiwei had a rough mastery of the Odes, Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, and Analects;

sentences.zh: 十八，師董道季講易；

translations.literal: at eighteen he studied the Changes under Dong Daoji;
translations.idiomatic: at eighteen he studied the Changes under Dong Daoji;

sentences.zh: 十九，師程玄讀禮經及春秋三傳。

translations.literal: at nineteen he studied under Cheng Xuan, reading the Classic of Rites and the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn.
translations.idiomatic: at nineteen he studied under Cheng Xuan, reading the Classic of Rites and the three commentaries on the Spring and Autumn.

sentences.zh: 周流儒肆，有名於冀方。

translations.literal: He moved through Confucian schools and was renowned in the Ji region.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled among Confucian schools and was renowned throughout the Ji region.

sentences.zh: 太和初，郡舉孝廉，對策於中書省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taihe his commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt; he answered imperial questions at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taihe era his commandery recommended him as Filial and Incorrupt, and he answered imperial questions at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時中書監高閭宿聞惠蔚，稱其英辯，因相談，薦為中書博士。

translations.literal: At that time Secretariat Supervisor Gao Lu had long heard of Huiwei and praised his eloquent brilliance; after conversing he recommended him as Secretariat doctoral chair.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Secretariat Supervisor Gao Lu had long heard of Huiwei and praised his eloquent brilliance. After conversing with him, Lu recommended him as Secretariat doctoral chair.

sentences.zh: 轉皇宗博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Imperial Clan doctoral chair.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Imperial Clan doctoral chair.

sentences.zh: 閭被敕理定雅樂，惠蔚參其事。

translations.literal: Lu received orders to arrange and fix the court music; Huiwei participated in the work.
translations.idiomatic: Lu received orders to arrange and fix the court music, and Huiwei participated in the work.

sentences.zh: 及樂成，閭上疏請集朝貴於太樂，共研是非。

translations.literal: When the music was complete Lu submitted a memorial requesting that court nobles be gathered at the Grand Music Office to examine right and wrong together.
translations.idiomatic: When the music was complete, Lu submitted a memorial requesting that court nobles be gathered at the Grand Music Office to debate its merits together.

sentences.zh: 祕書令李彪自以才辯，立難於其間，閭命惠蔚與彪抗論，彪不能屈。

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Li Biao, confident in his talent and eloquence, raised challenges in their midst; Lu ordered Huiwei to debate Li Biao, and Biao could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Director Li Biao, confident in his talent and eloquence, raised objections in their midst. Lu ordered Huiwei to debate him, and Biao could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎張彝常與遊處，每表疏論事，多參訪焉。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Zhang Yi often kept company with him; whenever submitting memorials to discuss affairs he frequently consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Zhang Yi often kept company with him and frequently consulted him when drafting memorials on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 十七年，高祖南征，上議告類之禮。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south; the court discussed the rites of announcing to Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Emperor Xiaowen campaigned south, and the court debated the rites of announcing victory to Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 及太師馮熙薨，惠蔚監其喪禮，上書令熙未冠之子皆服成人之服。

translations.literal: When Grand Preceptor Feng Xi died, Huiwei oversaw the mourning rites and submitted a memorial that Xi's sons who had not yet capped should wear the mourning garments of adults.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Preceptor Feng Xi died, Huiwei oversaw the mourning rites and submitted a memorial that Xi's sons who had not yet come of age should wear adult mourning garments.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚與李彪以儒學相知，及彪位至尚書，惠蔚仍太廟令。

translations.literal: Huiwei and Li Biao knew each other through Confucian learning; when Biao rose to Minister of the Secretariat, Huiwei remained Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Huiwei and Li Biao had become friends through their shared Confucian learning. When Biao rose to Minister of the Secretariat, Huiwei remained Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 高祖曾從容言曰：「道固既登龍門而孫蔚猶沉涓澮，朕常以為負矣。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowen once said at ease, "Daogu has already ascended the Dragon Gate while Sun Wei still sinks in a shallow ditch—I have always felt indebted over this."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen once remarked at leisure, "Daogu has already passed through the Dragon Gate while Sun Wei still lingers in a shallow ditch—I have always felt I owed him better."

sentences.zh: 」雖久滯小官，深體通塞，無孜孜之望，儒者以是尚焉。

translations.literal: " Though long stuck in minor office, he deeply understood the alternation of obstruction and success and harbored no restless ambition—Confucian scholars thereby held him in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Though long confined to minor office, he deeply understood the alternation of obstruction and success and harbored no restless ambition—Confucian scholars held him in esteem for this.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，侍讀東宮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he served as reader attendant in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he served as reader attendant in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 先是七廟以平文為太祖，高祖議定祖宗，以道武為太祖。

translations.literal: Previously the seven ancestral temples took Emperor Pingwen as High Ancestor; Emperor Xiaowen deliberated on fixing the ancestral line and took Emperor Daowu as High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the seven ancestral temples had taken Emperor Pingwen as High Ancestor. Emperor Xiaowen deliberated on fixing the imperial ancestors and made Emperor Daowu the High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 祖宗雖定，然昭穆未改。

translations.literal: Although the ancestral line was fixed, the zhao-mu order had not yet been changed.
translations.idiomatic: Although the imperial ancestors had been fixed, the zhao-mu temple order had not yet been adjusted.

sentences.zh: 及高祖崩，祔神主於廟，時侍中崔光兼太常卿，以太祖既改，昭穆以次而易。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowen died, the spirit tablets were enshrined in the temple; at that time Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang concurrently served as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and since the High Ancestor had been changed, the zhao-mu order was accordingly shifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowen died and his spirit tablet was enshrined in the ancestral temple, Attendant-in-Ordinary Cui Guang was concurrently serving as Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Since the designation of High Ancestor had changed, he reordered the zhao-mu positions accordingly.

sentences.zh: 兼御史中尉、黃門侍郎邢巒以為太祖雖改，昭穆仍不應易，乃立彈草欲按奏光。

translations.literal: Concurrently Inspector-in-Chief of the Censorate and Yellow Gate Attendant Xing Luan held that although the High Ancestor had been changed, the zhao-mu order still should not be altered; he therefore drafted an impeachment memorial intending to investigate and report Cui Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector-in-Chief of the Censorate and Yellow Gate Attendant Xing Luan argued that even though the High Ancestor had been changed, the zhao-mu order should not be altered. He drafted an impeachment memorial and prepared to bring charges against Cui Guang.

sentences.zh: 光謂惠蔚曰：「此乃禮也，而執法欲見彈劾，思獲助於碩學。

translations.literal: Guang said to Huiwei, "This is a matter of ritual, yet those who enforce the law wish to see me impeached—I am hoping to gain aid from a great scholar."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang said to Huiwei, "This is a matter of ritual, yet the law officers wish to impeach me. I hope I can rely on your help as a leading scholar."

sentences.zh: 」惠蔚曰：「此深得禮變。

translations.literal: " Huiwei said, "This truly grasps ritual change deeply."
translations.idiomatic: Huiwei said, "Your position accords deeply with the principle of adapting ritual to changed circumstances."

sentences.zh: 」尋為書以與光，讚明其事。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he wrote a letter to Guang, commending and clarifying the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He soon composed a letter for Guang, explaining and endorsing his position.

sentences.zh: 光以惠蔚書呈宰輔，乃召惠蔚與巒庭議得失，尚書令王肅又助巒，而巒理終屈，彈事遂寢。

translations.literal: Guang presented Huiwei's letter to the chief ministers; thereupon Huiwei and Luan were summoned to debate right and wrong in court; Minister of the Secretariat Wang Su again supported Luan, but Luan's argument was ultimately defeated and the impeachment was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guang submitted Huiwei's letter to the chief ministers. Huiwei and Xing Luan were then summoned to debate the matter in court. Minister of the Secretariat Wang Su again sided with Luan, but Luan's argument ultimately failed and the impeachment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位之後，仍在左右敷訓經典，自冗從僕射遷祕書丞、武邑郡中正。

translations.literal: After Emperor Xuanwu took the throne, he still remained at court to expound and teach the classics; he was promoted from Supernumerary Associate Master of Ceremonies to Secretariat Aide and Rectifier of Wuyi Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuanwu ascended the throne, Huiwei remained at court to expound the classics. He was promoted from Supernumerary Associate Master of Ceremonies to Secretariat Aide and Rectifier of Wuyi Commandery.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚既入東觀，見典籍未周，乃上疏曰：「臣聞聖皇之御世也，必幽贊人經，參天二地，憲章典故，述遵鴻猷。

translations.literal: Once Huiwei entered the Eastern Pavilion, seeing the classics were incomplete, he submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject has heard that when a sage emperor governs the age, he must deeply assist the human classics, match Heaven and Earth in dual harmony, take ancient precedents as his model, and follow the great design."
translations.idiomatic: Once Huiwei entered the Eastern Pavilion and saw that the collection of classics was incomplete, he submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that when a sage emperor governs the realm, he must exalt the human classics, harmonize with Heaven and Earth, take ancient precedents as his model, and follow the great design of governance."

sentences.zh: 故易曰：『觀乎天文以察時變，觀乎人文以化成天下。

translations.literal: Thus the Classic of Changes says: 'Observing the patterns of Heaven to discern the changes of the times; observing the patterns of culture to transform and complete the realm under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Classic of Changes says: 'Observe the patterns of Heaven to discern the changes of the times; observe the patterns of culture to transform and complete all under Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 』然則六經、百氏，圖書祕籍，乃承天之正術，治人之貞範。

translations.literal: " Thus the Six Classics, the hundred schools, diagrams, books, and secret archives are the orthodox arts by which Heaven is received and the true standard for governing people.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Classics, the hundred schools, and all books and secret archives are the orthodox arts handed down by Heaven and the true standard for governing the people.

sentences.zh: 是以溫柔疏遠，詩書之教；

translations.literal: Hence gentleness and yielding, distance and withdrawal—the teaching of the Poetry and Documents;
translations.idiomatic: From them come gentleness and reserve—the teaching of the Classic of Poetry and the Book of Documents;

sentences.zh: 恭儉易良，禮樂之道。

translations.literal: reverence and frugality, ease and goodness—the Way of ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: reverence and frugality, ease and goodness—the Way of ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 爻彖以精微為神，春秋以屬辭為化。

translations.literal: The hexagram lines and judgments take subtle precision as their spirit; the Spring and Autumn takes linked wording as its transformative power.
translations.idiomatic: In the Classic of Changes, subtle precision is the standard; in the Spring and Autumn Annals, linked wording is the means of transformation.

sentences.zh: 故大訓炳於東序，藝文光於麟閣。

translations.literal: Thus great instruction shines in the Eastern Side-chamber, and literary works gleam in the Qilin Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Thus great teachings shine in the Eastern Side-chamber of the palace, and literary works gleam in the Qilin Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 斯實太平之樞宗，勝殘之要道，有國之靈基，帝王之盛業。

translations.literal: This is truly the pivotal ancestor of great peace, the essential way to overcome cruelty, the numinous foundation of possessing a state, and the splendid enterprise of emperors and kings.
translations.idiomatic: This is truly the foundation of great peace, the essential means of overcoming cruelty, the living foundation of empire, and the supreme achievement of emperors and kings.

sentences.zh: 安上靖民，敦風美俗，其在茲乎？

translations.literal: To secure superiors and pacify the people, to solidify customs and beautify practices—is it not here?
translations.idiomatic: To secure the throne and pacify the people, to strengthen customs and refine morals—is this not their purpose?

sentences.zh: 及秦棄學術，禮經泯絕。

translations.literal: When Qin abandoned learning, the rites classics were extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Qin abandoned learning, the rites classics were all but lost.

sentences.zh: 漢興求訪，典文載舉，先王遺訓，燦然復存。

translations.literal: When Han rose it sought and enquired; canonical writings were again lifted up; the surviving instructions of the former kings blazed forth and were preserved anew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han dynasty rose, it searched far and wide for texts. Canonical writings were recovered, and the instructions of the former kings blazed forth once more.

sentences.zh: 暨光武撥亂，日不暇給，而入洛之書二千餘兩。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangwu settled the chaos, though his days allowed no respite, the books brought into Luoyang numbered more than two thousand cartloads.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Emperor Guangwu restored order amid chaos, though his days allowed no respite, more than two thousand cartloads of books were brought into Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 魏晉之世，尤重典墳，收亡集逸，九流咸備。

translations.literal: In the Wei-Jin age they especially valued the canon-tombs; gathering what was lost and collecting what was scattered, all nine traditions were fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wei and Jin periods learning was especially prized. Lost texts were collected and scattered works gathered in, until all nine intellectual traditions were represented.

sentences.zh: 觀其鳩閱史篇，訪購經論，紙竹所載，略盡無遺。

translations.literal: Observing how they assembled and reviewed historical records and sought and purchased classical treatises, what paper and bamboo bore was nearly complete without omission.
translations.idiomatic: They assembled and reviewed historical records, sought out and purchased classical treatises—hardly any text recorded on paper or bamboo was left uncollected.

sentences.zh: 臣學闕通儒，思不及遠，徒循章句，片義無立。

translations.literal: Your subject's learning falls short of the comprehensive Confucian; his thought does not reach far; he merely follows chapter and phrase and has established no fragment of meaning.
translations.idiomatic: My own learning falls short of true mastery, and my thought does not reach far. I merely follow chapter and phrase and have achieved nothing of substance.

sentences.zh: 而慈造曲覃，厠班祕省，忝官承乏，唯書是司。

translations.literal: Yet by your gracious creation he is deeply admitted and placed in rank within the secretariat; holding office he fills a vacancy and has charge only of books.
translations.idiomatic: Yet by your gracious favor I have been admitted to the Secretariat. I hold this office only to fill a vacancy, and my sole charge is the books.

sentences.zh: 而觀、閣舊典，先無定目，新故雜糅，首尾不全。

translations.literal: Yet the old classics of the Pavilion and Library previously had no fixed catalog; new and old were mixed in confusion and beginning and end were incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the old classics housed in the Pavilion and Library have no fixed catalog. New and old texts are jumbled together, and many works are incomplete from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 有者累帙數十，無者曠年不寫。

translations.literal: Some exist in accumulated fascicles numbering dozens; others for years on end have not been copied.
translations.idiomatic: Some exist in dozens of bundled fascicles; others have gone years without being copied.

sentences.zh: 或篇第褫落，始末淪殘；

translations.literal: Some have sections and sequence stripped away, beginning and end reduced to ruins;
translations.idiomatic: Some have lost sections and sequence, with beginnings and endings in ruins;

sentences.zh: 或文壞字誤，謬爛相屬。

translations.literal: some have damaged text and erroneous characters, errors and corruption following one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: others have damaged text and mistaken characters, errors and corruption piled one upon another.

sentences.zh: 篇目雖多，全定者少。

translations.literal: Though headings and items are many, complete and fixed copies are few.
translations.idiomatic: Though the catalog is long, complete and settled copies are few.

sentences.zh: 臣今依前丞臣盧昶所撰甲乙新錄，欲裨殘補闕，損併有無，校練句讀，以為定本，次第均寫，永為常式。

translations.literal: Your subject now wishes to follow the new A-B catalog compiled by former Aide Lu Chang, to repair what is damaged and supplement what is missing, reduce and merge what exists and what does not, collate and refine punctuation, make it the fixed edition, copy it in proper order, and establish it forever as the regular standard.
translations.idiomatic: I now propose to follow the new A-B catalog compiled by my predecessor, Secretariat Aide Lu Chang: to repair damaged passages, fill lacunae, consolidate duplicate and missing texts, collate punctuation, establish a definitive edition, copy it in proper order, and fix it as the permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 其省先無本者，廣加推尋，搜求令足。

translations.literal: For those in the secretariat previously without copies, extensively pursue and search until they are complete.
translations.idiomatic: For texts the Secretariat currently lacks, I would search widely until complete copies are obtained.

sentences.zh: 然經記浩博，諸子紛綸，部帙既多，章篇紕繆，當非一二校書，歲月可了。

translations.literal: Yet the classics and records are vast, the various masters numerous and tangled; sections and fascicles are already many and chapters and fascicles confused—this cannot be completed by one or two collators in months and years.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the classics are vast and the various masters numerous; with so many fascicles and so much confusion among chapters, this cannot be finished by one or two collators in a matter of months.

sentences.zh: 今求令四門博士及在京儒生四十人，在祕書省專精校考，參定字義。

translations.literal: Your subject now requests that forty Four Gates Doctors and Confucian scholars in the capital be assigned to the Secretariat to specialize in collation and verification and jointly fix the meanings of characters.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore request that forty Four Gates Doctors and Confucian scholars resident in the capital be assigned to the Secretariat to specialize in collation and jointly establish the correct readings.

sentences.zh: 如蒙聽許，則典文允正，羣書大集。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty graciously permits, then the canonical writings will be properly correct and the multitude of books greatly assembled.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty grants this request, the canonical texts will be properly corrected and the entire collection will be brought to order.

sentences.zh: 」詔許之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 又兼黃門侍郎，遷中散大夫，仍兼黃門。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Yellow Gate Attendant and promoted to Palace Regular Grandee, still concurrently serving as Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was additionally appointed Yellow Gate Attendant and promoted to Palace Regular Grandee, while retaining his post as Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 久之，正黃門侍郎，代崔光為著作郎，才非文史，無所撰著，唯自披其傳注數行而已。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made regular Yellow Gate Attendant, replacing Cui Guang as Director of Compilation; his talent was not for history and literature, and he composed nothing—only perused a few lines of his own commentarial writings.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was made regular Yellow Gate Attendant and replaced Cui Guang as Director of Compilation. He lacked talent for history and literature and produced no original work—he merely read through a few lines of his own commentaries.

sentences.zh: 遷國子祭酒、祕書監，仍知史事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chancellor of the National University and Director of the Secretariat Library, still overseeing historiographical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Chancellor of the National University and Director of the Secretariat Library, while continuing to oversee historiographical affairs.

sentences.zh: 延昌二年，追賞侍講之勞，封棗強縣開國男，食邑二百戶。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanbei, to reward his labors as reader-attendant, he was enfeoffed as Founding Baron of Zaoqiang County with a fief of two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yanbei his past service as court reader was rewarded: he was enfeoffed as Founding Baron of Zaoqiang County with a fief of two hundred households.

sentences.zh: 肅宗初，出為平東將軍、濟州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign, he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaoming's reign, he was sent out as General Who Pacifies the East and Governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 還京，除光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 魏初已來，儒生寒宦，惠蔚最為顯達。

translations.literal: From the beginning of Wei, among Confucian scholars of humble official origin, Huiwei was the most prominent.
translations.idiomatic: From the early Wei period onward, among Confucian scholars from modest backgrounds, none rose so high as Huiwei.

sentences.zh: 先單名蔚，正始中，侍講禁內，夜論佛經，有愜帝旨，詔使加「惠」，號惠蔚法師焉。

translations.literal: Previously he bore the single name Wei; in the Zhengshi era, lecturing within the forbidden precincts, he discussed Buddhist sutras at night; it pleased the emperor's intent, and an edict ordered the addition of "Hui," and he was styled Master Huiwei.
translations.idiomatic: He had originally borne the single name Wei. During the Zhengshi era, while lecturing within the inner palace, he discussed Buddhist sutras at night in a manner that pleased the emperor, who ordered the character "Hui" added to his name. He was thereafter known as Master Huiwei.

sentences.zh: 神龜元年卒于官，時年六十七。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenshen he died in office, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the first year of Shenshen, at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 賜帛五百匹，贈大將軍、[5]瀛州刺史，諡曰戴。

translations.literal: Five hundred bolts of silk were bestowed; he was posthumously granted General-in-Chief, [5] Governor of Yingzhou, with posthumous title Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred bolts of silk were bestowed upon his death. He was posthumously granted the title General-in-Chief and Governor of Yingzhou, [5] with the posthumous name Dai.

sentences.zh: 子伯禮，襲封。

translations.literal: His son Bolí succeeded to the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bolí inherited the enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 伯禮善隸書。

translations.literal: Bolí was skilled at clerical script.
translations.idiomatic: Bolí was skilled in clerical script.

sentences.zh: 拜奉朝請、員外散騎侍郎、寧朔將軍、步兵校尉、國子博士。

translations.literal: He was appointed Palace Attendant, Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the North, Commandant of Footsoldiers, and National University Doctor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Palace Attendant, Supernumerary Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary, General Who Pacifies the North, Commandant of Footsoldiers, and Doctor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈輔國將軍、巴州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously granted General Who Assists the State and Governor of Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously granted the title General Who Assists the State and Governor of Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 子產同，襲。

translations.literal: His son Chantong succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chantong inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 少有才學，早亡，時人惜之。

translations.literal: He had talent and learning in youth, died early, and people of the time regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: He showed talent and learning in youth but died young, to the regret of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 徐遵明，字子判，華陰人也。

translations.literal: Xu Zunming, courtesy name Zipan, was a man of Huayin.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zunming, courtesy name Zipan, was a native of Huayin.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，幼孤好學。

translations.literal: His stature was eight feet; orphaned in youth, he loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet tall. Orphaned in youth, he devoted himself to learning.

sentences.zh: 年十七，隨鄉人毛靈和等詣山東求學。

translations.literal: At age seventeen he followed fellow townsman Mao Linghe and others to go to Shandong to seek learning.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he set out with fellow townsman Mao Linghe and others for Shandong to pursue his studies.

sentences.zh: 至上黨，乃師屯留王聰，受毛詩、尚書、禮記。

translations.literal: Reaching Shangdang, he then took as master Wang Cong of Tunliu and received the Mao Odes, Documents, and Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Shangdang, he studied under Wang Cong of Tunliu, learning the Mao Commentary on the Odes, the Book of Documents, and the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 一年，便辭聰詣燕趙，師事張吾貴。

translations.literal: After one year he took leave of Cong and went to Yan and Zhao, taking as master Zhang Wugui.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he left Wang Cong and traveled to Yan and Zhao to study under Zhang Wugui.

sentences.zh: 吾貴門徒甚盛，遵明伏膺數月，乃私謂其友人曰：「張生名高而義無檢格，凡所講說，不愜吾心，請更從師。

translations.literal: Wugui's disciples were very numerous; Zunming bowed in submission for several months, then privately told his friend, "Master Zhang's fame is high but his conduct lacks restraint; everything he lectures does not satisfy my heart—I request to seek another teacher."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wugui's disciples were very numerous. Zunming studied under him for several months, then confided to a friend, "Master Zhang enjoys great renown but lacks proper restraint. None of his lectures satisfies me—I mean to find another teacher."

sentences.zh: 」遂與平原田猛略就范陽孫買德受業。

translations.literal: " Thereupon with Pingyuan's Tian Menglue he went to Fan Yang's Sun Maide to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: He then went with Tian Menglue of Pingyuan to study under Sun Maide of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 一年，復欲去之。

translations.literal: After one year he again wished to leave.
translations.idiomatic: After another year, he wished to leave again.

sentences.zh: 猛略謂遵明曰：「君年少從師，每不終業，千里負帙，何去就之甚。

translations.literal: Menglue said to Zunming, "You are young in following teachers, each time not completing your course; carrying your bundles a thousand li—why is your going and staying so extreme?"
translations.idiomatic: Menglue said to him, "You are still young, yet every time you study with a teacher you fail to finish. You carry your texts a thousand li—why are you so restless in coming and going?"

sentences.zh: 如此用意，終恐無成。

translations.literal: With intent such as this, in the end I fear you will accomplish nothing.
translations.idiomatic: With such restlessness, I fear you will never accomplish anything."

sentences.zh: 」遵明曰：「吾今始知真師所在。

translations.literal: " Zunming said, "I now begin to know where the true teacher resides."
translations.idiomatic: Zunming replied, "I have now discovered where the true teacher is."

sentences.zh: 」猛略曰：「何在？

translations.literal: " Menglue said, "Where?"
translations.idiomatic: Menglue asked, "Where is that?"

sentences.zh: 」遵明乃指心曰：「正在於此。

translations.literal: " Zunming then pointed to his heart and said, "Precisely here."
translations.idiomatic: Zunming pointed to his heart and said, "Right here."

sentences.zh: 」乃詣平原唐遷，納之，居於蠶舍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he went to Pingyuan's Tang Qian, who took him in, and he lived in a silkworm house.
translations.idiomatic: He then went to Tang Qian of Pingyuan, who took him in. He lived in a silkworm-rearing shed.

sentences.zh: 讀孝經、論語、毛詩、尚書、三禮，不出門院，凡經六年，時彈箏吹笛以自娛慰。

translations.literal: He read the Filial Classic, Analects, Mao Odes, Documents, and the Three Rites, not leaving gate or courtyard; altogether six years passed, at times plucking the zither and blowing the flute to amuse and comfort himself.
translations.idiomatic: He studied the Classic of Filial Piety, the Analects, the Mao Commentary on the Odes, the Book of Documents, and the Three Rites without leaving his courtyard. Six years passed in this way. At times he played the zither and flute to amuse himself.

sentences.zh: 又知陽平館陶趙世業家有服氏春秋，是晉世永嘉舊本，遵明乃往讀之。

translations.literal: He also learned that Zhao Shiye's household in Guantao, Yangping, possessed Fu's Spring and Autumn, an old edition from the Yongjia era of Jin; Zunming therefore went to read it.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhao Shiye's household in Guantao, Yangping, possessed Fu's Spring and Autumn Annals—an edition dating from the Yongjia era of the Jin—Zunming went there to study it.

sentences.zh: 復經數載，因手撰春秋義章，為三十卷。

translations.literal: After several more years he personally composed Explications of the Meaning of the Spring and Autumn, thirty fascicles in all.
translations.idiomatic: After several more years he composed his own Explications of the Spring and Autumn Annals in thirty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 是後教授，門徒蓋寡，久之乃盛。

translations.literal: Thereafter when he taught, disciples were generally few; only after a long time did they flourish.
translations.idiomatic: When he began to teach, his disciples were few; only after a long time did their numbers grow.

sentences.zh: 遵明每臨講坐，必持經執疏，然後敷陳，其學徒至今浸以成俗。

translations.literal: Whenever Zunming mounted the lecture seat he always held the classic and grasped the commentary, only then expounding; his disciples to this day have gradually made it custom.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zunming lectured he always held the classic in one hand and the commentary in the other before expounding—a practice his disciples have gradually turned into custom.

sentences.zh: 遵明講學於外二十餘年，海內莫不宗仰。

translations.literal: Zunming lectured abroad for more than twenty years; within the seas none did not revere and look up to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zunming taught abroad for more than twenty years, and scholars throughout the realm revered him.

sentences.zh: 頗好聚歛，有損儒者之風。

translations.literal: He rather loved amassing wealth, which damaged the manner of the Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: He was rather fond of amassing wealth, which somewhat tarnished his reputation as a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 後廣平王懷聞而徵焉。

translations.literal: Later Prince Huai of Guangping heard of him and summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prince Huai of Guangping heard of him and summoned him.

sentences.zh: 至而尋退，不好京輦。

translations.literal: When he arrived he soon withdrew, disliking the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived but soon withdrew, having no taste for life near the capital.

sentences.zh: 孝昌末，南渡河，客於任城。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaochong he crossed the river south and sojourned at Rencheng.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiaochong era he crossed the Yellow River to the south and took lodging at Rencheng.

sentences.zh: 以兗州有舊，因徙居焉。

translations.literal: Because he had old ties in Yanzhou, he thereupon moved to dwell there.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had old ties in Yan Province, he moved there to settle.

sentences.zh: 永安初，東道大使元羅表薦之，竟無禮辟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yong'an, Eastern Route Commissioner Yuan Luo memorialized recommending him, yet in the end no formal summons came.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yong'an, Eastern Route Commissioner Yuan Luo recommended him by memorial, but no official summons ever came.

sentences.zh: 二年，元顥入洛，任城太守李湛將舉義兵，遵明同其事。

translations.literal: In the second year Yuan Hao entered Luoyang; Rencheng Prefect Li Zhan was about to raise a righteous army, and Zunming joined in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Yuan Hao entered Luoyang. Rencheng Prefect Li Zhan was preparing to raise a loyalist force, and Zunming joined the effort.

sentences.zh: 夜至民間，為亂兵所害，時年五十五。

translations.literal: At night he came among the common people and was killed by disorderly troops; he was fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: That night, while among the common people, he was killed by marauding soldiers. He was fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，遵明弟子通直散騎常侍李業興表曰：「臣聞行道樹德，非求利於當年；

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Zunming's disciple Direct-and-Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Yexing submitted a memorial saying, "Your subject has heard that practicing the Way and planting virtue is not seeking profit in one's own years;"
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi, Zunming's disciple Direct-and-Regular Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Li Yexing submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard that practicing the Way and cultivating virtue is not done for profit in one's own lifetime;"

sentences.zh: 服義履仁，豈邀恩於沒世。

translations.literal: wearing righteousness and treading benevolence—how could one invite grace after death?
translations.idiomatic: embracing righteousness and practicing benevolence is not done to seek favor after death."

sentences.zh: 但天爵所存，果致式閭之禮；

translations.literal: Yet when Heaven's rank is preserved, it truly brings the rite of marking the lane;
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Heaven's rank endures in a man, the rite of honoring his lane is indeed bestowed;

sentences.zh: 民望攸屬，終有祠墓之榮。

translations.literal: the people's expectation attaches to him, and in the end he has the glory of temple and tomb.
translations.idiomatic: when the people's hopes rest upon him, he ultimately receives the honor of temple and tomb.

sentences.zh: 伏見故處士兗州徐遵明生在衡泌，弗因世族之基；

translations.literal: Your subject humbly observes that the late retired scholar of Yanzhou Xu Zunming was born beside Heng and Bi and did not rely on the foundations of a great clan;
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe that the late recluse Xu Zunming of Yan Province was born beside the Heng and Bi streams and owed nothing to a great clan;

sentences.zh: 長於原野，匪乘雕鏤之地。

translations.literal: growing up in field and plain, not riding upon carved and inlaid ground.
translations.idiomatic: he grew up in open country, not on inlaid and carved floors.

sentences.zh: 而託心淵曠，置情恬雅，處靜無悶，居約不憂。

translations.literal: Yet he entrusted his heart to profound vastness, set his feelings in quiet elegance, dwelt in stillness without vexation, lived in simplicity without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he set his heart on depths and vast spaces, kept his spirit tranquil and refined, lived in quiet without vexation, and in poverty without distress.

sentences.zh: 故能垂簾自精，下帷獨得，鑽經緯之微言，研聖賢之妙旨。

translations.literal: Thus he could let down the curtain and refine himself alone, lower the curtain and gain understanding by himself, bore into the subtle words of the classics' warp and weft, and study the wondrous intent of sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he could study behind drawn curtains in solitary refinement, penetrating the subtle words of the classics and mastering the profound intent of sages and worthies.

sentences.zh: 莫不入其門戶，踐其堂奧，信以稱大儒於海內，擅明師於日下矣。

translations.literal: None failed to enter his gate and tread his inner hall—truly he could be called a great Confucian within the seas and a renowned master under the sun.
translations.idiomatic: Countless scholars entered his gate and reached the inner sanctum of his teaching. Truly he could be called the greatest Confucian of the realm and the preeminent master of his age.

sentences.zh: 是故眇眇四方，知音之類，延首慕德，跂踵依風。

translations.literal: Therefore from the distant four directions, those who understood music, craned their necks admiring virtue and stood on tiptoe following the wind.
translations.idiomatic: From every corner of the realm, those who understood his worth craned their necks in admiration and hastened to follow his example.

sentences.zh: 每精廬暫闢，杖策不遠千里；

translations.literal: Whenever his refined hut was briefly opened, with staff in hand they did not consider a thousand li far;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he opened his humble school, disciples would travel a thousand li without hesitation;

sentences.zh: 束脩受業，編錄將踰萬人。

translations.literal: bringing dried meat to receive instruction, those registered approached ten thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: bearing gifts of initiation to receive instruction—those enrolled in his records approached ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 固已企盛烈於西河，擬高蹤於北海。

translations.literal: Already he looked to the splendid achievements at Xihé and measured himself against the lofty traces at Beihai.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements already rivaled those of the great schools of Xihe, and his stature approached that of the masters of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 若慕奇好士，愛客尊賢，罷吏遊梁，紛而成列。

translations.literal: As for those who admired the extraordinary, loved scholars, cherished guests, and honored worthies, dismissed officials who wandered to Liang—they flocked and formed ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Like those who admire the extraordinary, love scholars, honor guests, and revere the worthy—dismissed officials flocking to join the great patrons—they gathered in ranks.

sentences.zh: 遵明以碩德重名，首蒙禮命，曳裾雅步，眷同置醴。

translations.literal: Zunming, by his great virtue and weighty fame, was first to receive ritual summons; trailing his hem with elegant step, he was cherished as if wine were placed before him.
translations.idiomatic: Zunming, by his great virtue and eminent reputation, was first to receive a formal summons. He was welcomed with honor, as though fine wine had been placed before a guest of distinction.

sentences.zh: 黃門李郁具所知明，方申薦奏之恩，處心守壑之志，潛居樂道，遂往不歸。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate Attendant Li Yu fully knew his clarity; just as he was about to extend the grace of recommendation and memorial, Zunming harbored the resolve to guard the ravine, dwelt in seclusion delighting in the Way, and went away never to return.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate Attendant Li Yu understood him well and was about to extend the grace of recommendation when Zunming, resolved to keep to his secluded life, chose quiet study and the Way over office—and departed never to return.

sentences.zh: 故北海王入洛之初，率土風靡，遵明確然守志，忠潔不渝，遂與太守李湛將誅叛逆。

translations.literal: Therefore when the Prince of Beihai first entered Luoyang, the whole realm was swept away; Zunming resolutely kept his resolve, loyal and pure without change, and thereupon with Prefect Li Zhan planned to execute the rebel.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Beihai first entered Luoyang and the whole land was swept up in the revolt, Zunming steadfastly held to his principles, loyal and incorruptible. He joined Prefect Li Zhan in planning to suppress the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時有邂逅，受斃凶險。

translations.literal: At that time there was a chance encounter; he received death amid danger and violence.
translations.idiomatic: By cruel chance he encountered marauding soldiers and met a violent death.

sentences.zh: 至誠高節，堙沒無聞，朝野人士，相與嗟悼。

translations.literal: His utmost sincerity and lofty integrity were buried in obscurity without renown; court and countryside figures together sighed and mourned.
translations.idiomatic: Such sincerity and lofty integrity, yet buried in obscurity without public recognition—men of court and countryside alike mourned him.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下遠應龍序，俯執天衷，每端聽而忘昃，常坐思而候曉。

translations.literal: Your subject humbly considers that Your Majesty far responds to the dragon's sequence and bowing holds Heaven's inner intent; each time you listen upright and forget the setting sun, constantly sit in thought and await the dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty responds to Heaven's mandate from afar and holds the true intent of governance. You listen with full attention past sunset and sit in contemplation awaiting the dawn.

sentences.zh: 雖微功小善，片言一行，莫不衣裳加室，玉帛在門。

translations.literal: Though merit be slight and goodness small, a single word or act—none fails to receive robes added to the chamber and jade silks at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Even the slightest merit or smallest good deed, a single word or act—none goes unrewarded with honors at your door.

sentences.zh: 況遵明冠蓋一時，師表當世，溘焉冥沒，旌紀寂寥。

translations.literal: Moreover Zunming stood foremost among officials of his age, a teacher and model for the world, yet suddenly passed into darkness and oblivion—his banners and record lie desolate.
translations.idiomatic: And Xu Zunming had stood at the head of his generation, a teacher and exemplar for the age—yet he was suddenly gone, leaving his honors and memorials all but forgotten.

sentences.zh: 逝者長辭，無論榮價，文明敍物，敦厲斯在。

translations.literal: The departed has long taken leave; regardless of glory and rank, civilizing and ordering things—earnest exhortation lies in this.
translations.idiomatic: The dead are gone forever; rank and glory aside, what matters is to civilize the world and put things in order—to inspire earnest striving is the point.

sentences.zh: 臣託跡諸生，親承顧眄，惟伏膺之義，感在三之重，是以越分陳愚，上諠幄座。

translations.literal: Your subject has placed himself among the students and personally received his gracious gaze; cherishing the duty of reverence and feeling the weight of the threefold bond of kindness, I therefore overstep my station to set forth my humble view, raising it before the imperial curtain.
translations.idiomatic: I myself studied under him and received his personal attention. Bound by reverence and deeply moved by the threefold debt of kindness, I overstep my station to offer this humble plea and lay it before Your Majesty's throne.

sentences.zh: 特乞加以顯諡，追以好爵，仰申朝廷尚德之風，下示學徒稽古之利。

translations.literal: I humbly beg that he be granted a distinguished posthumous title and rewarded with noble rank—thereby upholding above the court's esteem for virtue and showing below students the benefit of studying the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be granted a distinguished posthumous title and noble rank in recognition—upholding the court's esteem for virtue above and showing students below the rewards of classical learning.

sentences.zh: 若宸鑒昭回，曲垂矜採，則荒墳千載，式貴生平。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty's sage insight shines clear and you deign to show compassionate favor, then though his neglected grave endure a thousand years, his lifetime will be honored in perpetuity.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty's sage judgment looks favorably upon this and shows compassionate acceptance, then even a neglected grave a thousand years hence will stand as lasting honor to his life.

sentences.zh: 」卒無贈諡。

translations.literal: In the end no posthumous gifts or title were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the end no posthumous honors or title were granted.

sentences.zh: 董徵，字文發，頓丘衞國人也。

translations.literal: Dong Zheng, courtesy name Wenfa, was a native of Dunqiu in Weiguo.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zheng, courtesy name Wenfa, was a native of Dunqiu in Weiguo.

sentences.zh: 祖英，高平太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ying was Administrator of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ying served as Administrator of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 父虬，郡功曹。

translations.literal: His father Qiu was Merit Officer of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qiu was Merit Officer of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 徵身長七尺二寸，好古，學尚雅素。

translations.literal: Zheng stood seven chi two cun in height, loved antiquity, and in learning esteemed refinement and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng stood seven chi two cun tall. He loved antiquity and pursued learning in a spirit of refined simplicity.

sentences.zh: 年十七，師清河監伯陽，受論語、毛詩、春秋、周易，就河內高望崇受周官，後於博陵劉獻之遍受諸經。

translations.literal: At seventeen he took as master Jian Boyang of Qinghe and received instruction in the Analects, Mao's Odes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Book of Changes; he then went to Gao Wangchong of Henei to receive the Rites of Zhou, and afterward studied all the classics comprehensively under Liu Xianzhi of Boling.
translations.idiomatic: At seventeen he studied under Jian Boyang of Qinghe, learning the Analects, Mao's Odes, the Spring and Autumn Annals, and the Book of Changes. He then went to Gao Wangchong of Henei for the Rites of Zhou, and later studied the full canon under Liu Xianzhi of Boling.

sentences.zh: 數年之中，大義精練，講授生徒。

translations.literal: Within a few years he had mastered the great principles with refined thoroughness and lectured to students.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he had mastered the great principles of the classics and began lecturing to students.

sentences.zh: 太和末，為四門小學博士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Taihe era he served as Erudite of the Four Gates Primary School.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Taihe era he was appointed Erudite of the Four Gates Primary School.

sentences.zh: 後世宗詔徵入琁華宮，令孫惠蔚問以六經，仍詔徵教授京兆、清河、廣平、汝南四王，後特除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Xuanwu summoned Zheng into the Xuanhua Palace and had Sun Huiwei question him on the Six Classics; he also ordered Zheng to instruct the four princes of Jingzhao, Qinghe, Guangping, and Runan, and afterward specially appointed him Supernumerary Gentleman of the Palace Cadet.
translations.idiomatic: Later Emperor Xuanwu summoned Zheng to the Xuanhua Palace and had Sun Huiwei examine him on the Six Classics. He also ordered Zheng to instruct the four princes of Jingzhao, Qinghe, Guangping, and Runan, and later specially appointed him Supernumerary Gentleman of the Palace Cadet.

sentences.zh: 清河王懌之為司空、司徒，引徵為長流參軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Qinghe, Yi, served as Minister of Works and then Minister over the Masses, he recruited Zheng as Senior Adjutant of the Flowing Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qinghe, Yi, served as Minister of Works and then Minister over the Masses, he recruited Zheng as Senior Adjutant of the Flowing Staff.

sentences.zh: 懌遷太尉，徵為倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Yi was transferred to Grand Commandant, Zheng became Adjutant of the Granary Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi was promoted to Grand Commandant, Zheng became Adjutant of the Granary Bureau.

sentences.zh: 出為沛郡太守，加揚烈將軍。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Administrator of Pei Commandery and was additionally appointed General Who Displays Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Administrator of Pei Commandery with the additional title General Who Displays Majesty.

sentences.zh: 入為太尉司馬，俄加輔國將軍。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Major of the Grand Commandant and soon received the additional title General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the capital as Major of the Grand Commandant and was soon given the additional title General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以本將軍除安州刺史。

translations.literal: Before long, retaining his general's title, he was appointed Inspector of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Inspector of Anzhou, retaining his general's rank.

sentences.zh: 徵因述職，路次過家，置酒高會，大享邑老，乃言曰：「腰龜返國，昔人稱榮；

translations.literal: Zheng, on his way to report on his duties, passed by his home and set out wine for a grand gathering, feasting the elders of his district. He then said, "Returning to one's state with a turtle insignia at the waist—men of old called this glory;
translations.idiomatic: On his way to take up his post, Zheng passed through his home district. He held a grand feast for the local elders and said, "To return to one's homeland wearing the turtle insignia of high office—men of old counted that glory;

sentences.zh: 仗節還家，云胡不樂。

translations.literal: returning home bearing the imperial staff—how could one not rejoice?"
translations.idiomatic: to return home bearing the imperial staff—why should one not rejoice?"

sentences.zh: 」因誡二三子弟曰：「此之富貴，匪自天降，乃勤學所致耳。

translations.literal: He then admonished two or three of the younger kinsmen, saying, "This wealth and eminence did not fall from Heaven—it came from diligent study alone."
translations.idiomatic: He then admonished his younger relatives: "This wealth and rank did not fall from Heaven—they came from diligent study alone."

sentences.zh: 」時人榮之。

translations.literal: Men of the time honored him for it.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 入為司農少卿、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Court of the National Granaries and as Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as Vice Director of the Court of the National Granaries and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 徵出州入卿，匪唯學業所致，亦由汝南王悅以其師資之義，為之啟請焉。

translations.literal: Zheng's rise from provincial office to court minister was not due to scholarship alone; the Prince of Runan, Yue, also petitioned on his behalf out of the bond between teacher and pupil.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's rise from provincial office to court minister owed not only to his scholarship—the Prince of Runan, Yue, also petitioned on his behalf out of respect for their bond as teacher and pupil.

sentences.zh: 永安初，加平東將軍，尋以老解職。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he received the additional title General Who Pacifies the East, and soon afterward resigned on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yong'an era he was given the additional title General Who Pacifies the East, and soon resigned on account of age.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Yongxi.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Yongxi.

sentences.zh: 出帝以徵昔授父業，故優贈散騎常侍、都督相殷滄三州諸軍事、車騎大將軍、儀同三司、尚書左僕射、相州刺史，諡曰文烈。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaojing, because Zheng had once instructed his father, generously posthumously granted him Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs in the three provinces of Xiang, Yin, and Cang, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Xiangzhou, with the posthumous title Wenlie.
translations.idiomatic: Because Zheng had once been his father's teacher, Emperor Xiaojing generously posthumously honored him as Palace Attendant, Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Xiang, Yin, and Cang provinces, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Inspector of Xiangzhou, with the posthumous title Wenlie.

sentences.zh: 子仲曜，武定末，儀同開府屬。

translations.literal: His son Zhongyao, at the end of the Wuding era, served as an aide in an office equal in honor to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhongyao served at the end of the Wuding era as an aide in a ducal-level office.

sentences.zh: 刁沖，字文朗，勃海饒安人也，鎮東將軍雍之曾孫。

translations.literal: Diao Chong, courtesy name Wenlang, was a native of Rao'an in Bohai and great-grandson of General Who Guards the East Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Diao Chong, courtesy name Wenlang, was a native of Rao'an in Bohai and the great-grandson of General Who Guards the East Yong.

sentences.zh: 十三而孤，孝慕過人。

translations.literal: Orphaned at thirteen, his filial grief exceeded that of others.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at thirteen, his filial devotion and grief exceeded that of ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 其祖母司空高允女，聰明婦人也，哀其早孤，撫養尤篤。

translations.literal: His grandmother was a daughter of Minister of Works Gao Yun—a clever woman who pitied his early orphanhood and raised him with especial devotion.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother was a daughter of Minister of Works Gao Yun—a wise woman who pitied his early orphanhood and raised him with exceptional devotion.

sentences.zh: 沖免喪後便志學他方，高氏泣涕留之，沖終不止。

translations.literal: After Chong completed mourning he resolved to study elsewhere; the Gao clan wept and pleaded to keep him, but Chong would not be deterred.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong's mourning period ended he resolved to study elsewhere. The Gaos wept and begged him to stay, but he would not be turned aside.

sentences.zh: 雖家世貴達，乃從師於外，自同諸生。

translations.literal: Though his family for generations had been noble and eminent, he went outside to follow teachers and placed himself on equal footing with the other students.
translations.idiomatic: Though his family had been noble and eminent for generations, he went abroad to study under teachers and lived no differently from the other students.

sentences.zh: 於時學制，諸生悉日直監厨，沖雖有僕隸，不令代己，身自炊爨。

translations.literal: Under the school regulations of the time, all students took daily turns supervising the kitchen; though Chong had servants, he would not let them replace him and cooked for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Under the school rules of the time, every student took daily turns supervising the kitchen. Though Chong had servants, he would not let them stand in for him and cooked for himself.

sentences.zh: 每師受之際，發情精專，不捨晝夜，殆忘寒暑。

translations.literal: Whenever he received instruction from his teachers he poured forth his spirit in concentrated devotion, never ceasing day or night, nearly forgetting cold and heat.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he studied under his teachers he gave himself wholly to the work, never resting day or night, scarcely noticing cold or heat.

sentences.zh: 學通諸經，偏修鄭說，陰陽、圖緯、算數、天文、風氣之書莫不關綜，當世服其精博。

translations.literal: He mastered all the classics, specializing in the Zheng interpretive tradition, and comprehensively connected works on yin and yang, chart-weft lore, mathematics, astronomy, and wind-and-qi—men of his age admired his profound breadth.
translations.idiomatic: He mastered the full canon, specializing in the Zheng Xuan school, and ranged across works on yin and yang, prognostic lore, mathematics, astronomy, and wind and qi. Contemporaries admired his depth and breadth.

sentences.zh: 刺史郭祚聞其盛名，訪以疑義，沖應機解辯，無不祛其久惑。

translations.literal: Inspector Guo Zuo heard of his great reputation and consulted him on points of doubt; Chong responded on the spot with explanation and debate, always dispelling long-standing confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector Guo Zuo heard of his fame and consulted him on difficult points. Chong answered on the spot, always clearing away doubts that had long persisted.

sentences.zh: 後太守范陽盧尚之、刺史河東裴植並徵沖為功曹、[6]主簿，非所好也，受署而已，不關事務。

translations.literal: Later Prefect Lu Shangzhi of Fanyang and Inspector Pei Zhi of Hedong both summoned Chong as Merit Officer [6] and Chief Clerk—posts not to his liking; he accepted appointment only in name and did not involve himself in administrative affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prefect Lu Shangzhi of Fanyang and Inspector Pei Zhi of Hedong both summoned Chong to serve as Merit Officer [6] and Chief Clerk—posts he did not care for. He accepted the titles in name only and took no part in administrative affairs.

sentences.zh: 惟以講學為心，四方學徒就其受業者歲有數百。

translations.literal: He devoted himself solely to lecturing; students who came from all directions to study under him numbered several hundred each year.
translations.idiomatic: Teaching was his sole concern. Each year several hundred students came from all directions to study under him.

sentences.zh: 沖雖儒生，而執心壯烈，不畏強禦。

translations.literal: Though Chong was a Confucian scholar, his resolve was bold and fierce and he did not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Though a Confucian scholar, Chong had a bold and resolute heart and did not fear the powerful.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，世宗舅司徒高肇擅恣威權，沖乃抗表極言其事，辭旨懇直，文義忠憤。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era, Emperor Xuanwu's maternal uncle, Minister over the Masses Gao Zhao, arrogantly wielded power at will; Chong submitted a memorial boldly stating the matter in full—the wording earnest and direct, the meaning loyal and indignant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yanchang era, Emperor Xuanwu's maternal uncle Gao Zhao, Minister over the Masses, wielded power with arrogant impunity. Chong submitted a memorial speaking out boldly—the language earnest and direct, the tone loyal and indignant.

sentences.zh: 太傅、清河王懌覽而歎息。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor, the Prince of Qinghe Yi, read it and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor, the Prince of Qinghe Yi, read it and sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 先是沖曾祖雍作行孝論以誡子孫，稱：「古之葬者衣之以薪，不封不樹，後世聖人易之棺椁。

translations.literal: Earlier Chong's great-grandfather Yong wrote an Essay on Filial Conduct in Burial to admonish his descendants, saying, "The ancients in burial clothed the dead in firewood, neither sealing mounds nor planting trees; later sages replaced this with coffins and outer cases.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Chong's great-grandfather Yong had written an Essay on Filial Conduct in Burial to instruct his descendants, saying, "The ancients clothed the dead in firewood for burial, neither raising mounds nor planting trees; later sages replaced this with coffins and outer cases.

sentences.zh: 其有生則不能致養，死則厚葬過度。

translations.literal: Yet while the living they could not provide proper support; in death they buried with excessive lavishness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet while their parents lived they failed to provide proper care, and in death they buried them with excessive extravagance.

sentences.zh: 及於末世，至蘧蒢裹尸，倮而葬者。

translations.literal: By the age of decline there were even those who wrapped corpses in coarse grass mats and buried them naked.
translations.idiomatic: By the decadent age some went so far as to wrap corpses in coarse grass mats and bury them naked.

sentences.zh: 確而為論，並非折衷。

translations.literal: To insist on either extreme in making one's argument is not true moderation.
translations.idiomatic: To take either extreme as doctrine is not true moderation.

sentences.zh: 既知二者之失豈宜同之。

translations.literal: Since one knows the failings of both, how can one follow either alike?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the failings of both, how can one follow either to the same degree?

sentences.zh: 當令所存者棺厚不過三寸，高不過三尺，弗用繒綵，斂以時服。

translations.literal: What should remain is this: coffin thickness no more than three cun, height no more than three chi; no use of colored silks; enshroud in the garments worn in life.
translations.idiomatic: What should remain is this: coffins no more than three cun thick and three chi high; no colored silks; the dead should be dressed in their ordinary clothes.

sentences.zh: 轜車止用白布為幔，不加畫飾，名為清素車。

translations.literal: The funeral carriage should use only white cloth for its canopy, with no painted ornament, and be called the Plain and Simple Carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral carriage should use only a white cloth canopy, with no painted decoration—a carriage called the Plain and Simple Hearse.

sentences.zh: 又去挽歌、方相，并盟器雜物。

translations.literal: Also remove dirges, exorcism-mask figures, and grave goods and miscellaneous objects.
translations.idiomatic: Also remove dirges, exorcism-mask figures, grave goods, and other such objects.

sentences.zh: 」及沖祖遵將卒，敕其子孫令奉雍遺旨。

translations.literal: When Chong's grandfather Zun was about to die, he charged his descendants to follow Yong's last instructions.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong's grandfather Zun was near death, he charged his descendants to follow Yong's last instructions.

sentences.zh: 河南尹丞張普惠謂為太儉，貽書於沖叔整議其進退。

translations.literal: Assistant to the Intendant of Henan Zhang Puhui considered this too austere and sent a letter to Chong's uncle Zheng to discuss whether to follow it or not.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant to the Intendant of Henan Zhang Puhui considered the rites too austere and wrote to Chong's uncle Zheng to debate whether to follow them.

sentences.zh: 整令與通學議之，沖乃致書國學諸儒以論其事，學官竟不能答。

translations.literal: Zheng had fellow students discuss the matter; Chong then sent a letter to the Confucian scholars of the Imperial Academy to debate the issue, and the academy officials in the end could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng had fellow students discuss the matter. Chong then wrote to the Confucian scholars of the Imperial Academy to argue the case, and the academy officials could not answer him.

sentences.zh: 沖以嫡傳祖爵東安侯。

translations.literal: Chong as the legitimate heir inherited his grandfather's title Marquis of Dong'an.
translations.idiomatic: As legitimate heir, Chong inherited his grandfather's title, Marquis of Dong'an.

sentences.zh: 京兆王繼為司空也，並以高選頻辟記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jingzhao Ji served as Minister of Works, he repeatedly recruited Chong, selecting him for excellence, as Recorder of the Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Jingzhao Ji served as Minister of Works, he repeatedly recruited Chong for his outstanding talent as Recorder of the Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 肅宗將親釋奠，於是國子助教韓神固與諸儒詣國子祭酒崔光、吏部尚書甄琛，舉其才學，奏而徵焉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaoming was about to personally perform the vegetable-offering ceremony, Assistant Erudite of the Imperial University Han Sheng and the Confucian scholars went to Imperial Academy Chancellor Cui Guang and Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Zhen Chen to recommend Chong's talent and learning; a memorial was submitted and he was summoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaoming was about to perform the Confucian vegetable-offering ceremony in person, Imperial University Assistant Erudite Han Sheng and other scholars went to Chancellor Cui Guang of the Imperial Academy and Minister of Personnel Zhen Chen to recommend Chong's talent and learning. A memorial was submitted and he was summoned.

sentences.zh: 及卒，國子博士高涼及范陽盧道侃、[7]盧景裕等復上狀陳沖業行，議奏諡曰安憲先生，祭以太牢。

translations.literal: When he died, Imperial University Erudite Gao Liang and Lu Daokan [7] of Fanyang, Lu Jingyu, and others again submitted a memorial describing Chong's achievements and conduct; it was deliberated and memorialized that he be given the posthumous title Master Anxian, with sacrifice of the highest grade.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, Imperial University Erudite Gao Liang, Lu Daokan [7] of Fanyang, Lu Jingyu, and others submitted a memorial describing Chong's achievements and conduct. The court deliberated and granted him the posthumous title Master Anxian, with sacrifice of the highest grade.

sentences.zh: 子欽，字志儒。

translations.literal: His son Qin, courtesy name Zhiru.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qin, courtesy name Zhiru.

sentences.zh: 早亡。

translations.literal: He died young.
translations.idiomatic: He died young.

sentences.zh: 盧景裕，字仲儒，小字白頭，范陽涿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Jingyu, courtesy name Zhongru, childhood name Baitou, was a native of Zhuo in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Jingyu, courtesy name Zhongru, childhood name Baitou, was a native of Zhuo in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 章武伯同之兄子。

translations.literal: He was a nephew of Marquis of Zhangwu Tong.
translations.idiomatic: He was a nephew of Marquis of Zhangwu Tong.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏，專經為學。

translations.literal: From youth he was clever and quick, dedicating himself to the classics in his studies.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was clever and quick, dedicating himself to the study of the classics.

sentences.zh: 居拒馬河，將一老婢作食，妻子不自隨從。

translations.literal: He lived by the Juma River, keeping one old maidservant to prepare food; his wife and children did not accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived by the Juma River with only an old maidservant to cook for him; his wife and children did not live with him.

sentences.zh: 又避地大寧山，不營世事，居無所業，惟在注解。

translations.literal: He also withdrew to Mount Daning, did not pursue worldly affairs, had no occupation in his dwelling, and devoted himself solely to commentary.
translations.idiomatic: He also withdrew to Mount Daning, took no part in worldly affairs, and had no occupation beyond writing commentaries.

sentences.zh: 其叔父同職居顯要，而景裕止於園舍，情均郊野，謙恭守道，貞素自得。

translations.literal: Though his uncle Tong held an eminent and important post, Jingyu remained in his garden dwelling, his feelings equal to those of the countryside, humble and reverent in keeping to the Way, chaste and plain and content in himself.
translations.idiomatic: Though his uncle Tong held an eminent post, Jingyu remained in his garden retreat, as content as a man of the fields—humble, devoted to the Way, and quietly satisfied in plain living.

sentences.zh: 由是世號居士。

translations.literal: For this reason the world called him the Recluse.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason people called him the Recluse.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝初，除國子博士，參議正聲，甚見親遇，待以不臣之禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the reign of the Deposed Emperor, he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University and participated in deliberating the standard musical tones; he was greatly favored and treated with the ceremony due one who need not bow as subject.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Deposed Emperor's reign he was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University and took part in deliberating the standard musical tones. He was greatly favored and treated with the ceremony reserved for one who need not bow as a subject.

sentences.zh: 永熙初，以例解。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongxi he was dismissed according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yongxi he was dismissed from office according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 天平中，還鄉里，與邢子才、魏季景、魏收、邢昕等同徵赴鄴。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he returned to his home district and, together with Xing Zicai, Wei Jijing, Wei Shou, and Xing Xin, was summoned together to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he returned home and was summoned to Ye together with Xing Zicai, Wei Jijing, Wei Shou, and Xing Xin.

sentences.zh: 景裕寓託僧寺，講聽不已。

translations.literal: Jingyu lodged in a Buddhist monastery and never ceased lecturing and listening.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu lodged in a Buddhist monastery and never ceased lecturing and attending discussions.

sentences.zh: 未幾，歸本郡。

translations.literal: Before long he returned to his home commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to his home commandery.

sentences.zh: 河間邢摩納與景裕從兄仲禮據鄉作逆，逼其同反，以應元寶炬。

translations.literal: Xing Mona of Hejian and Jingyu's older cousin Zhongli seized their district in rebellion, forcing others to join the revolt in response to Yuan Baoju.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Mona of Hejian and Jingyu's older cousin Zhongli seized their district in rebellion, forcing others to join them in support of Yuan Baoju.

sentences.zh: 齊獻武王命都督賀拔仁討平之。

translations.literal: Prince Xianwu of Qi ordered Area Commander Heba Ren to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xianwu of Qi ordered Area Commander Heba Ren to suppress the rebellion.
