sentences.zh: 聞景裕經明行著，驛馬特徵，既而舍之，使教諸子。

translations.literal: Hearing that Jingyu was clear in the classics and distinguished in conduct, he sent post-horses to summon him specially; then he released him and had him instruct his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Jingyu was distinguished in both learning and conduct, he sent post-horses to summon him specially, then released him and had him instruct his sons.

sentences.zh: 在館十日一歸家，隨以鼎食。

translations.literal: While at the residence he returned home once every ten days and was provided with sumptuous fare.
translations.idiomatic: While living at the residence he returned home once every ten days and was provided with lavish meals.

sentences.zh: 景裕風儀言行，雅見嗟賞。

translations.literal: Jingyu's bearing, speech, and conduct were greatly admired.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu's bearing, speech, and conduct won high admiration.

sentences.zh: 先是景裕注周易、尚書、孝經、論語、禮記、老子，其毛詩、春秋左氏未訖。

translations.literal: Earlier Jingyu had commented on the Book of Changes, Book of Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Record of Rites, and Laozi; his commentaries on Mao's Odes and the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals were unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu had already completed commentaries on the Book of Changes, Book of Documents, Classic of Filial Piety, Analects, Record of Rites, and Laozi; his commentaries on Mao's Odes and the Zuo Tradition of the Spring and Autumn Annals remained unfinished.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄王入相，於第開講，招延時儁，令景裕解所注易。

translations.literal: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi entered the chancellorship, he opened lectures at his residence, invited eminent men of the age, and had Jingyu expound his commentary on the Changes.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Wenxiang of Qi became chancellor, he held lectures at his residence, invited eminent scholars of the age, and had Jingyu expound his commentary on the Changes.

sentences.zh: 景裕理義精微，吐發閑雅。

translations.literal: Jingyu's principles and meanings were subtle and refined; his delivery was easy and elegant.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyu's reasoning was subtle and refined, and his delivery calm and elegant.

sentences.zh: 時有問難，或相詆訶，大聲厲色，言至不遜，而景裕神彩儼然，風調如一，從容往復，無際可尋。

translations.literal: At times there were challenges and questions; some reviled one another, raising their voices and showing harsh color, speaking to the point of insolence—yet Jingyu's spirit and expression remained composed, his tone unchanged; he responded at ease back and forth with no opening to be found.
translations.idiomatic: When challengers pressed him, some shouted abuse with harsh voices and insolent words—yet Jingyu remained composed, his tone unchanged, answering at ease with no opening for attack.

sentences.zh: 由是士君子嗟美之。

translations.literal: For this reason gentlemen sighed in admiration of him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and gentlemen admired him greatly for it.

sentences.zh: 初，元顥入洛，[8]以為中書郎。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, [8] he was appointed Palace Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yuan Hao entered Luoyang, [8] Jingyu was appointed Palace Secretary.

sentences.zh: 普泰初，復除國子博士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Putai he was again appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Putai he was again appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 進退其間，未曾有得失之色。

translations.literal: Through advance and retreat in this period he never showed the color of gain or loss.
translations.idiomatic: Through all these changes of fortune he never showed pleasure or distress.

sentences.zh: 性清靜，淡於榮利，弊衣粗食，恬然自安，終日端嚴，如對賓客。

translations.literal: By nature he was quiet and pure, indifferent to glory and profit; in worn clothes and coarse food he was content and at peace, all day upright and solemn as though receiving guests.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was quiet and pure, indifferent to rank and profit. In worn clothes and plain food he was content, maintaining all day a dignified bearing as though receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 興和中，補齊王開府屬，卒於晉陽，齊獻武王悼惜之。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era he was appointed aide in the office of the Prince of Qi and died at Jinyang; Prince Xianwu of Qi mourned and regretted his loss.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xinghe era he was appointed aide in the Prince of Qi's office. He died at Jinyang, and Prince Xianwu of Qi mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 景裕雖不聚徒教授，所注易大行於世。

translations.literal: Though Jingyu did not gather disciples to teach, his commentary on the Changes circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jingyu did not gather disciples to teach, his commentary on the Changes circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 又好釋氏，通其大義。

translations.literal: He also loved Buddhism and mastered its great principles.
translations.idiomatic: He also loved Buddhism and mastered its essential teachings.

sentences.zh: 天竺胡沙門道悕每論諸經論，輒託景裕為之序。

translations.literal: The Indian monk Daoxi, whenever he discussed the various sutras and treatises, always entrusted Jingyu to write prefaces for them.
translations.idiomatic: The Indian monk Daoxi always asked Jingyu to write prefaces whenever he lectured on the sutras and treatises.

sentences.zh: 景裕之敗也。

translations.literal: When Jingyu met with calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingyu fell into adversity.

sentences.zh: 繫晉陽獄，至心誦經，枷鎖自脫。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned in the jail at Jinyang; chanting sutras with utmost sincerity, his cangue and fetters fell away of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He was imprisoned in the jail at Jinyang. Chanting sutras with utmost devotion, his cangue and fetters fell away by themselves.

sentences.zh: 是時又有人負罪當死，夢沙門教講經，覺時如所夢，默誦千遍，臨刑刀折，主者以聞，赦之。

translations.literal: At that time there was also a man guilty of a capital crime who dreamed a monk taught him to recite a sutra; upon waking he did as in the dream and silently recited it a thousand times; at execution the blade broke, the official in charge reported it, and he was pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: At that time another man condemned to death dreamed that a monk taught him to recite a sutra. Upon waking he did as in the dream and silently recited it a thousand times. At execution the blade broke; the official reported this and he was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 此經遂行於世，號曰高王觀世音。

translations.literal: This sutra then circulated in the world and was called the Guanyin of the King of Gao.
translations.idiomatic: This sutra then spread widely and came to be known as the Guanyin Sutra of the King of Gao.

sentences.zh: 李同軌，趙郡高邑人，陽夏太守義深之弟。

translations.literal: Li Tonggui was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery and younger brother of Yishen, Administrator of Yangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tonggui was a native of Gaoyi in Zhao Commandery and the younger brother of Yishen, Administrator of Yangxia.

sentences.zh: 體貌魁岸，腰帶十圍，學綜諸經，多所治誦，兼讀釋氏，又好醫術。

translations.literal: His physique was imposing and lofty, his waist ten wei in girth; he mastered all the classics and had studied and recited many of them, also read Buddhist works, and loved medical arts.
translations.idiomatic: He had an imposing physique and a waist ten wei around. He mastered the classics and had studied and recited many of them, also read Buddhist texts, and loved medicine.

sentences.zh: 年二十二，舉秀才，射策，除奉朝請，領國子助教。

translations.literal: At twenty-two he was nominated as Outstanding Talent, passed the archery-and-policy examination, was appointed Palace Attendant, and served concurrently as Assistant Erudite of the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-two he was nominated as Outstanding Talent, passed the policy examination, was appointed Palace Attendant, and served concurrently as Assistant Erudite of the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 轉著作郎，典儀注，修國史，遷國子博士，加征虜將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Palace Library, directed ritual protocols, compiled the national history, was promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University, and received the additional title General Who Subdues Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Palace Library, directed ritual protocols, and compiled the national history. He was then promoted to Erudite of the Imperial University with the additional title General Who Subdues Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 永熙二年，出帝幸平等寺，僧徒講法，敕同軌論難，音韻閑朗，往復可觀，出帝善之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Xiaojing visited Pingdeng Temple; the monks expounded the Dharma and he ordered Tonggui to debate; his tones were easy and clear, his exchanges worth viewing, and Emperor Xiaojing approved of him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi, Emperor Xiaojing visited Pingdeng Temple while monks were expounding the Dharma. He ordered Tonggui to engage in debate. Tonggui's voice was clear and measured, his exchanges impressive, and the emperor was pleased.

sentences.zh: 三年春，釋菜，詔延公卿學官於顯陽殿，敕祭酒劉廞講孝經，黃門李郁講禮記，中書舍人盧景宣解大戴禮夏小正篇。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year, at the vegetable-offering ceremony, an edict summoned the high ministers and academy officials to the Xianyang Hall; the Chancellor Liu Yin was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Yellow Gate Attendant Li Yu on the Record of Rites, and Palace Secretary Attendant Lu Jingxuan to expound the Xiaxiaozheng chapter of Dai the Elder's Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year, at the Confucian vegetable-offering ceremony, an edict summoned high ministers and academy officials to the Xianyang Hall. Chancellor Liu Yin was ordered to lecture on the Classic of Filial Piety, Yellow Gate Attendant Li Yu on the Record of Rites, and Palace Secretary Attendant Lu Jingxuan to expound the Xiaxiaozheng chapter of Dai the Elder's Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時廣招儒學，引令預聽。

translations.literal: At the time Confucian learning was broadly recruited, and he was invited to attend and listen in advance.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court was broadly recruiting Confucian scholars, and Tonggui was invited to attend and listen.

sentences.zh: 同軌經義素優，辯析兼美，而不得執經，深為慨恨。

translations.literal: Tonggui had always been excellent in Classic meaning and equally fine in debate and analysis, yet he could not hold the lectern himself—he deeply regretted this.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggui had long excelled in the meaning of the classics and was equally gifted in debate, yet he was never given the lectern himself—a source of deep regret.

sentences.zh: 天平中，轉中書侍郎。

translations.literal: During Tianping, he was transferred to Palace Secretary Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianping era he was transferred to the post of Palace Secretary Attendant.

sentences.zh: 興和中，兼通直散騎常侍，使蕭衍。

translations.literal: During Xinghe, he additionally served as Regular Attendant of the Privy Staff and went as envoy to Xiao Yan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xinghe era he additionally served as Regular Attendant of the Privy Staff and was sent as envoy to Xiao Yan.

sentences.zh: 衍深耽釋學，遂集名僧於其愛敬、同泰二寺，講𣵀盤大品經，引同軌預席。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan was deeply devoted to Buddhist learning; he gathered renowned monks at his Ai'jing and Tongtai monasteries to expound the Mahaparinirvana Great Vaipulya Sutra and invited Tonggui to take a seat.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan was deeply devoted to Buddhist learning. He gathered eminent monks at his Ai'jing and Tongtai monasteries to expound the Mahaparinirvana Great Vaipulya Sutra and invited Tonggui to join the assembly.

sentences.zh: 衍兼遣其朝臣並共觀聽。

translations.literal: Xiao Yan also sent his court officials together to observe and listen.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan also sent his court officials to observe and listen together.

sentences.zh: 同軌論難久之，道俗咸以為善。

translations.literal: Tonggui debated at length; both clergy and laypeople all considered it excellent.
translations.idiomatic: Tonggui debated at length, and both clergy and laypeople alike praised his performance.

sentences.zh: 盧景裕卒，齊獻武王引同軌在館教諸公子，甚加禮之。

translations.literal: When Lu Jingyu died, King Xianwu of Qi brought Tonggui into his household to teach the princes and treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: After Lu Jingyu died, King Xianwu of Qi brought Tonggui into his household to instruct the princes and treated him with exceptional respect.

sentences.zh: 每旦入授，日暮始歸。

translations.literal: Each morning he would enter to instruct; only at dusk would he return.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning he entered to teach and did not return until dusk.

sentences.zh: 緇素請業者，同軌夜為說解，四時恒爾，不以為倦。

translations.literal: Those who sought instruction, whether monks or laypeople, Tonggui would expound and explain for them at night; he did this constantly through all four seasons and never wearied of it.
translations.idiomatic: For those who sought instruction, whether monks or laypeople, Tonggui would lecture and explain at night. He did this through all four seasons without ever tiring of it.

sentences.zh: 武定四年夏卒，年四十七。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year of Wuding he died, aged forty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the summer of the fourth year of Wuding, at the age of forty-seven.

sentences.zh: 時人傷惜之，齊獻武王亦殊嗟悼，贈襚甚厚。

translations.literal: People of the time mourned him; King Xianwu of Qi also lamented him especially, and the gifts for the dead were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time mourned his loss. King Xianwu of Qi also grieved for him deeply, and the funeral gifts were exceptionally generous.

sentences.zh: 贈驃騎大將軍、瀛州刺史，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General-in-Chief of Rapid Cavalry and Inspector of Ying Prefecture, with the posthumous title Kang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the titles General-in-Chief of Rapid Cavalry and Inspector of Ying Prefecture, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 李業興，上黨長子人也。

translations.literal: Li Yexing was a native of Changzi in Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yexing was a native of Changzi in Shangdang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖虬，父玄紀，並以儒學舉孝廉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiu and his father Xuanji both were nominated as Filial and Incorrupt through Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiu and his father Xuanji had both been nominated as Filial and Incorrupt on the strength of their Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 玄紀卒於金鄉令。

translations.literal: Xuanji died while serving as Magistrate of Jinxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanji died while serving as magistrate of Jinxiang.

sentences.zh: 業興少耿介，志學精力，負帙從師，不憚勤苦。

translations.literal: Yexing from youth was upright and self-possessed, aspired to learning with great energy, carried his book bundles to follow teachers, and was unafraid of toil and hardship.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yexing was upright and resolute. He pursued learning with great energy, carrying his books to follow his teachers and never shrinking from toil or hardship.

sentences.zh: 耽思章句，好覽異說。

translations.literal: He immersed himself in textual commentary and loved to read divergent interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: He immersed himself in textual commentary and loved to read divergent interpretations.

sentences.zh: 晚乃師事徐遵明於趙魏之間。

translations.literal: Only later did he take Xu Zunming as his teacher between Zhao and Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did he take Xu Zunming as his teacher in the region between Zhao and Wei.

sentences.zh: 時有漁陽鮮于靈馥亦聚徒教授，而遵明聲譽未高，著錄尚寡。

translations.literal: At the time Xianyu Lingfu of Yuyang also gathered disciples to teach, while Xu Zunming's reputation was not yet high and his enrollment was still small.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Xianyu Lingfu of Yuyang also gathered disciples to teach, while Xu Zunming's reputation was not yet established and his enrollment remained small.

sentences.zh: 業興乃詣靈馥黌舍，類受業者。

translations.literal: Yexing then went to Lingfu's school, resembling one seeking instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing then went to Lingfu's school, appearing for all the world like an ordinary student.

sentences.zh: 靈馥乃謂曰：「李生久逐羌博士，何所得也？

translations.literal: Lingfu then said to him, "Scholar Li, you have long followed the Qiang Doctor—what have you gained from it?
translations.idiomatic: Lingfu then said to him, "Scholar Li, you have long followed the Qiang Doctor—what have you learned from him?

sentences.zh: 」業興默爾不言。

translations.literal: " Yexing silently said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing said nothing and remained silent.

sentences.zh: 及靈馥說左傳，業興問其大義數條，靈馥不能對。

translations.literal: When Lingfu lectured on the Zuo Commentary, Yexing asked several questions on its broad meaning, which Lingfu could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: When Lingfu lectured on the Zuo Commentary, Yexing asked several questions about its broader meaning, which Lingfu could not answer.

sentences.zh: 於是振衣而起曰：「羌弟子正如此耳！

translations.literal: Thereupon Yexing shook out his robes and rose, saying, "A disciple of the Qiang is just like this!
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yexing shook out his robes and rose, saying, "A disciple of the Qiang is just like this!

sentences.zh: 」遂便徑還。

translations.literal: " Then he went straight back.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he went straight home.

sentences.zh: 自此靈馥生徒傾學而就遵明。

translations.literal: From this Lingfu's students all abandoned their studies and went to Xu Zunming.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, Lingfu's students abandoned him and flocked to Xu Zunming.

sentences.zh: 遵明學徒大盛，業興之為也。

translations.literal: Xu Zunming's disciples flourished greatly—this was Yexing's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zunming's following grew immensely—and it was Yexing who made it happen.

sentences.zh: 後乃博涉百家，圖緯、風角、天文、占候無不詳練，尤長算歷。

translations.literal: Later he broadly mastered the hundred schools; cosmological apocrypha, wind-direction divination, astronomy, and prognostication—none were beyond his detailed mastery; he was especially expert in calendrical calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Later he mastered a wide range of learning. Cosmological apocrypha, wind-direction divination, astronomy, and prognostication—none lay beyond his detailed command—and he was especially expert in calendrical calculation.

sentences.zh: 雖在貧賤，常自矜負，若禮待不足，縱於權貴，不為之屈。

translations.literal: Though poor and lowly, he constantly held himself in high regard; if he felt the courtesy shown insufficient, even before the powerful and noble he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Though poor and of humble station, he held himself in high regard. If he felt he had not been shown sufficient courtesy, he would not yield even to the powerful and noble.

sentences.zh: 後為王遵業門客。

translations.literal: Later he became a retainer in the household of Wang Zunye.
translations.idiomatic: Later he became a retainer in the household of Wang Zunye.

sentences.zh: 舉孝廉，為校書郎。

translations.literal: Nominated as Filial and Incorrupt, he became Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as Filial and Incorrupt, he was appointed Proofreader.

sentences.zh: 以世行趙𢾺曆，節氣後辰下算，延昌中，業興乃為戊子元曆上之。

translations.literal: Because the Zhao calendar then in use lagged the solar terms in its celestial calculations, during Yanchang Yexing composed the Wuzi Origin Calendar and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Zhao calendar then in use lagged behind the solar terms in its calculations, during the Yanchang era Yexing composed the Wuzi Origin Calendar and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 於時屯騎校尉張洪、盪寇將軍張龍祥等九家各獻新曆，世宗詔令共為一曆。

translations.literal: At that time Commandant of Attendant Cavalry Zhang Hong, General Who Quells Bandits Zhang Longxiang, and nine families in all each submitted new calendars; Emperor Shizong ordered them combined into one calendar.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Commandant of Attendant Cavalry Zhang Hong, General Who Quells Bandits Zhang Longxiang, and eight other families each submitted new calendars. Emperor Shizong ordered that they be combined into a single calendar.

sentences.zh: 洪等後遂共推業興為主，成戊子曆，[9]正光三年奏行之。

translations.literal: Hong and the others later jointly recommended Yexing as lead, completing the Wuzi Calendar, [9] which was submitted and put into use in the third year of Zhenguang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong and the others later jointly recommended Yexing to lead the effort, completing the Wuzi Calendar. [9] It was submitted and put into use in the third year of Zhenguang.

sentences.zh: 事在律曆志。

translations.literal: The matter is recorded in the Treatise on Calendars and Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The matter is recorded in the Treatise on Calendars and Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 累遷奉朝請。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 臨淮王彧征蠻，引為騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: When Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu campaigned against the southern barbarians, he recruited Yexing as Cavalry Army Adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Linhuai Yuan Yu campaigned against the southern barbarians, he recruited Yexing as Cavalry Army Adjutant.

sentences.zh: 後廣陵王淵北征，復為外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Later when Prince of Guangling Yuan Yuan campaigned north, he again served as Adjutant of External Troops.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Prince of Guangling Yuan Yuan campaigned north, he again served as Adjutant of External Troops.

sentences.zh: 業興以殷曆甲寅，黃帝辛卯，徒有積元，術數亡缺，業興又修之，各為一卷，傳於世。

translations.literal: Yexing held that the Yin Calendar of the Jiayin era and the Yellow Emperor Xinyin calendar had accumulated origin-years only in name while their calendrical methods were missing and defective; Yexing revised them, each in one scroll, and they were transmitted in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing held that the Yin Calendar of the Jiayin era and the Yellow Emperor Xinyin calendar possessed accumulated origin-years in name only, while their calendrical methods were lost and defective. He revised them, each in one scroll, and they were handed down in the world.

sentences.zh: 建義初，敕典儀注，未幾除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was ordered to direct ritual protocols; before long he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyi era he was ordered to direct ritual protocols. Before long he was appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 永安二年，以前造曆之勳，賜爵長子伯。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yong'an, for his earlier merit in creating the calendar, he was granted the title Marquis of Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yong'an, for his earlier merit in creating the calendar, he was granted the title Marquis of Changzi.

sentences.zh: 遭憂解任，尋起復本官。

translations.literal: He resigned on mourning leave, then soon returned to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned to observe mourning, then soon returned to his original post.

sentences.zh: 元曄之竊號也，除通直散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When Yuan Ye usurped the imperial title, he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Privy Staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Ye usurped the imperial title, Yexing was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Privy Staff.

sentences.zh: 普泰元年，沙汰侍官，業興仍在通直，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putai, when attendant officials were culled, Yexing remained in the Privy Staff with the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putai, when attendant officials were culled, Yexing retained his post in the Privy Staff and received the additional title General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 又除征虜將軍、中散大夫，仍在通直。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Palace Attendant Grandee, still serving in the Privy Staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed General Who Pacifies the Barbarians and Palace Attendant Grandee, while continuing to serve in the Privy Staff.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，轉散騎侍郎，仍以典儀之勤，特賞一階，除平東將軍、光祿大夫，尋加安西將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taichang he was transferred to Attendant Cavalry Gentleman; for his diligence in directing rituals he was specially rewarded one rank and appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Household Grandee; soon after he received the additional title General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taichang era he was transferred to Attendant Cavalry Gentleman. For his diligence in directing rituals he was specially rewarded one rank and appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Household Grandee; soon after he received the additional title General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 後以出帝登極之初，預行禮事，封屯留縣開國子，食邑五百戶。

translations.literal: Later, because at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's accession he participated in ritual affairs, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Tunliu with an estate of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Later, because he had taken part in ritual affairs at the beginning of Emperor Xiaowu's accession, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Tunliu with an estate of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 轉中軍將軍、通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Central Army and Regular Attendant of the Privy Staff.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General of the Central Army and Regular Attendant of the Privy Staff.

sentences.zh: 永熙三年二月，出帝釋奠，業興與魏季景、溫子昇、竇瑗為摘句。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year of Yongxi, at Emperor Xiaowu's Confucian temple sacrifice, Yexing together with Wei Jijing, Wen Zisheng, and Dou Yuan served as excerpt presenters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year of Yongxi, at Emperor Xiaowu's Confucian temple sacrifice, Yexing served as excerpt presenter together with Wei Jijing, Wen Zisheng, and Dou Yuan.

sentences.zh: 後入為侍讀。

translations.literal: Later he entered court as Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered court service as Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 遷鄴之始，起部郎中辛術奏曰：「今皇居徙御，百度創始，營構一興，必宜中制。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the move to Ye, Director of the Bureau of Construction Xin Shu memorialized, saying, "Now the imperial residence is being relocated and every measure is being newly established; once construction begins, it must conform to the central standard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the move to Ye, Director of the Bureau of Construction Xin Shu memorialized, saying, "Now that the imperial residence is being relocated and every institution is being newly established, once construction begins it must conform to a central standard.

sentences.zh: 上則憲章前代，下則模寫洛京。

translations.literal: Above, it should take the former dynasties as its model; below, it should replicate Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Above, it should take the former dynasties as its model; below, it should replicate the layout of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 今鄴都雖舊，基址毀滅，又圖記參差，事宜審定。

translations.literal: Now though Ye is an old capital, its foundations have been destroyed, and the maps and records are inconsistent—the matter requires careful determination.
translations.idiomatic: Although Ye is an old capital, its foundations have been destroyed, and the maps and records are inconsistent. The matter requires careful determination.

sentences.zh: 臣雖曰職司，學不稽古，國家大事非敢專之。

translations.literal: Though I hold this office, my learning does not reach back to antiquity, and I dare not decide a matter of such national importance on my own.
translations.idiomatic: Though I hold this office, my learning does not reach back to antiquity, and I dare not decide a matter of such national importance on my own.

sentences.zh: 通直散騎常侍李業興碩學通儒，博聞多識，萬門千戶，所宜訪詢。

translations.literal: Regular Attendant of the Privy Staff Li Yexing is a great scholar and thorough Confucian, broad in learning and rich in knowledge—the myriad gates and thousand households are matters he should be consulted on.
translations.idiomatic: Regular Attendant of the Privy Staff Li Yexing is a great scholar and thorough Confucian, broad in learning and rich in knowledge. Matters of palace layout and urban design are precisely what he should be consulted about.

sentences.zh: 今求就之披圖案記，考定是非，參古雜今，折中為制，召畫工并所須調度，具造新圖，申奏取定。

translations.literal: I now request that he be sent for to examine the maps and records, determine what is correct and incorrect, compare antiquity with the present and strike a mean as the standard, summon painters together with whatever supplies are needed, fully produce new plans, and submit them for approval.
translations.idiomatic: I now request that he be summoned to examine the maps and records, determine what is correct and incorrect, compare antiquity with the present and strike a balanced standard, summon painters together with whatever supplies are needed, produce complete new plans, and submit them for imperial approval.

sentences.zh: 庶經始之日，執事無疑。

translations.literal: Thus on the day construction begins, those in charge will have no doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when construction begins, those in charge will have no doubts.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: " An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 天平二年，除鎮南將軍，尋為侍讀。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianping he was appointed General Who Guards the South; soon after he became Lecturer-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianping he was appointed General Who Guards the South; soon after he became Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 於時尚書右僕射、營構大將高隆之被詔繕治三署樂器、衣服及百戲之屬，乃奏請業興共參其事。

translations.literal: At that time Executive Assistant of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi, commissioned as Grand General of Construction, received an edict to repair the instruments, garments, and variety-show accoutrements of the Three Bureaus; he then memorialized asking that Yexing jointly participate in the matter.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Executive Assistant of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi, commissioned as Grand General of Construction, received an edict to repair the instruments, garments, and variety-show accoutrements of the Three Bureaus. He then memorialized asking that Yexing participate jointly in the work.

sentences.zh: 四年，與兼散騎常侍李諧、[10]兼吏部郎盧元明使蕭衍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went as envoy to Xiao Yan together with Concurrent Regular Attendant of Attendant Cavalry Li He, [10] and Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Yuanming.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he went as envoy to Xiao Yan together with Concurrent Regular Attendant of Attendant Cavalry Li He, [10] and Concurrent Director of the Ministry of Personnel Lu Yuanming.

sentences.zh: 衍散騎常侍朱异問業興曰：「魏洛中委粟山是南郊邪？

translations.literal: Xiao Yan's Regular Attendant of Attendant Cavalry Zhu Yi asked Yexing, "In Wei Luoyang, is Mount Weisu the Southern Suburb?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan's Regular Attendant of Attendant Cavalry Zhu Yi asked Yexing, "In Wei Luoyang, is Mount Weisu the Southern Suburb?

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「委粟是圓丘，非南郊。

translations.literal: " Yexing said, "Weisu is the Round Mound, not the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing said, "Weisu is the Round Mound, not the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 」异曰：「北間郊、丘異所，是用鄭義。

translations.literal: " Yi said, "In the North the suburban altar and the mound are at separate sites—this follows Zheng Xuan's interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi said, "In the North the suburban altar and the mound are at separate sites—that follows Zheng Xuan's interpretation.

sentences.zh: 我此中用王義。

translations.literal: Here among us we follow Wang Su's interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: Here we follow Wang Su's interpretation.

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「然，洛京郊、丘之處專用鄭解。

translations.literal: " Yexing said, "Indeed—in Luoyang the sites of the suburban altar and the mound exclusively follow Zheng's explanation.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing said, "Indeed—in Luoyang the sites of the suburban altar and the mound exclusively follow Zheng's explanation.

sentences.zh: 」异曰：「若然，女子逆降傍親亦從鄭以不？

translations.literal: " Yi said, "If so, in the matter of a woman's descending in mourning rank for collateral relatives, do you also follow Zheng?
translations.idiomatic: " Yi said, "If so, in the matter of a woman's descending in mourning rank for collateral relatives, do you also follow Zheng?

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「此之一事，亦不專從。

translations.literal: " Yexing said, "In this one matter, we do not exclusively follow him either.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing said, "In this one matter, we do not exclusively follow him either.

sentences.zh: 若卿此間用王義，除禫應用二十五月，何以王儉喪禮禫用二十七月也？

translations.literal: If here among you Wang's interpretation is followed, the end of mourning should come in the twenty-fifth month—so why did Wang Jian's Mourning Rites prescribe the twenty-seventh month for ending mourning?
translations.idiomatic: If here you follow Wang's interpretation, the end of mourning should come in the twenty-fifth month—so why did Wang Jian's Mourning Rites prescribe the twenty-seventh month for ending mourning?

sentences.zh: 」异遂不答。

translations.literal: " Yi then made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi made no reply.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「我昨見明堂四柱方屋，都無五九之室，當是裴頠所制。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "Yesterday I saw the Bright Hall—a square hall on four pillars—with none of the five-by-nine chambers; it must be the design of Pei Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said, "Yesterday I saw the Bright Hall—a square hall on four pillars—with none of the five-by-nine chambers. It must be the design of Pei Yin.

sentences.zh: 明堂上圓下方，裴唯除室耳。

translations.literal: The Bright Hall is round above and square below; Pei only removed the chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The Bright Hall is round above and square below; Pei only removed the chambers.

sentences.zh: 今此上不圓何也？

translations.literal: Why is this one not round above?
translations.idiomatic: Why is this one not round above?

sentences.zh: 」异曰：「圓方之說，經典無文，何怪於方？

translations.literal: " Yi said, "The round-and-square doctrine has no textual basis in the classics—what is strange about square?
translations.idiomatic: " Yi said, "The round-and-square doctrine has no textual basis in the classics—what is strange about square?

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「圓方之言，出處甚明，卿自不見。

translations.literal: " Yexing said, "The round-and-square doctrine is very clearly attested in its sources—you simply have not seen them.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing said, "The round-and-square doctrine is very clearly attested in its sources—you simply have not seen them.

sentences.zh: 見卿錄梁主孝經義亦云上圓下方，卿言豈非自相矛盾！

translations.literal: I see that in your record of the Liang ruler's Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety it also says round above and square below—are your words not self-contradictory!
translations.idiomatic: I see that in your record of the Liang ruler's Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety it also says round above and square below—are your words not self-contradictory!

sentences.zh: 」异曰：「若然，圓方竟出何經？

translations.literal: " Yi said, "If so, from which classic does the round-and-square doctrine ultimately come?
translations.idiomatic: " Yi said, "If so, from which classic does the round-and-square doctrine ultimately come?

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「出孝經援神契。

translations.literal: " Yexing said, "It comes from the Apocryphal Text on the Classic of Filial Piety Supporting the Divine Covenant.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing said, "It comes from the Apocryphal Text on the Classic of Filial Piety Supporting the Divine Covenant.

sentences.zh: 」异曰：「緯候之書，何用信也！

translations.literal: " Yi said, "Why should one trust books of cosmological apocrypha and prognostication!
translations.idiomatic: " Yi said, "Why should one trust books of cosmological apocrypha and prognostication!

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「卿若不信，靈威仰、叶光紀之類經典亦無出者，卿復信不？

translations.literal: " Yexing said, "If you do not believe, texts like the Lingweiyang and the Yeguangji likewise have no attestation in the classics—do you believe in them or not?
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing said, "If you do not believe, texts like the Lingweiyang and the Yeguangji likewise have no attestation in the classics—do you believe in them or not?

sentences.zh: 」异不答。

translations.literal: " Yi made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Yi made no reply.

sentences.zh: 蕭衍親問業興曰：「聞卿善於經義，儒、玄之中何所通達？

translations.literal: Xiao Yan personally asked Yexing, "I hear you are skilled in Classic meaning—in Confucian and Dark Learning alike, what do you comprehend?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yan personally asked Yexing, "I hear you are skilled in the meaning of the classics—in Confucian and Dark Learning alike, what do you comprehend?

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「少為書生，止讀五典，至於深義，不辨通釋。

translations.literal: " Yexing said, "In youth I was a scholar who read only the Five Classics; as for their deeper meaning, I cannot distinguish or explain it thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing said, "In youth I was a scholar who read only the Five Classics. As for their deeper meaning, I cannot distinguish or explain it thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 」衍問：「詩周南，王者之風，繫之周公；

translations.literal: " Yan asked, "In the Poetry, Zhou Nan is the air of the kingly way and is attributed to the Duke of Zhou;
translations.idiomatic: " Yan asked, "In the Poetry, Zhou Nan is the air of the kingly way and is attributed to the Duke of Zhou;

sentences.zh: 邵南，仁賢之風，繫之邵公。

translations.literal: Shao Nan is the air of humane worthies and is attributed to the Duke of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Nan is the air of humane worthies and is attributed to the Duke of Shao.

sentences.zh: 何名為繫？

translations.literal: What is meant by 'attributed'?
translations.idiomatic: What is meant by 'attributed'?

sentences.zh: 」業興對曰：「鄭注儀禮云：昔大王、王季居于岐陽，躬行邵南之教，以興王業。

translations.literal: " Yexing replied, "Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Ceremonies and Rites says: In former times King Da and King Ji dwelt at Qiyang and personally carried out the teachings of Shao Nan to raise up the royal enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing replied, "Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Ceremonies and Rites says: In former times King Da and King Ji dwelt at Qiyang and personally carried out the teachings of Shao Nan to raise up the royal enterprise.

sentences.zh: 及文王行今周南之教以受命。

translations.literal: When King Wen carried out the teachings of Zhou Nan as they are today, he received the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When King Wen carried out the teachings of Zhou Nan as they are today, he received the Mandate.

sentences.zh: 作邑於酆，分其故地，屬之二公。

translations.literal: He established his capital at Feng and divided the former territory, assigning portions to the two dukes.
translations.idiomatic: He established his capital at Feng and divided the former territory, assigning portions to the two dukes.

sentences.zh: 名為繫。

translations.literal: This is what is meant by 'attributed.'
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant by 'attributed.'

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「若是故地，應自統攝，何由分封二公？

translations.literal: " Yan asked again, "If it was former territory, he should have governed it himself—how could he enfeoff the two dukes?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan asked again, "If it was former territory, he should have governed it himself—how could he enfeoff the two dukes?

sentences.zh: 」業興曰：「文王為諸侯之時所化之本國，今既登九五之尊，不可復守諸侯之地，故分封二公。

translations.literal: " Yexing said, "It was the homeland over which Wen had exercised transforming influence while still a feudal lord. Now that he had ascended to the Nine-Five position of supreme dignity, he could no longer hold feudal territory himself, and so he enfeoffed the two dukes.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing said, "It was the homeland over which Wen had exercised transforming influence while still a feudal lord. Now that he had ascended to supreme dignity, he could no longer hold feudal territory himself, and so he enfeoffed the two dukes.

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「乾卦初稱『潛龍』，二稱『見龍』，至五『飛龍』。

translations.literal: " Yan asked again, "In the Qian hexagram the first line is called 'Hidden Dragon,' the second 'Dragon Appears,' and by the fifth 'Flying Dragon.'
translations.idiomatic: " Yan asked again, "In the Qian hexagram the first line is called 'Hidden Dragon,' the second 'Dragon Appears,' and by the fifth 'Flying Dragon.'

sentences.zh: 初可名為虎。

translations.literal: The first could be called a tiger.
translations.idiomatic: The first could be called a tiger.

sentences.zh: 」問意小乖。

translations.literal: " The intent of the question was slightly off.
translations.idiomatic: The intent of the question was slightly off.

sentences.zh: 業興對：「學識膚淺，不足仰酬。

translations.literal: Yexing replied, "My learning is shallow and superficial—not adequate to meet your question worthily.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing replied, "My learning is shallow and superficial—not adequate to meet your question worthily.

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「尚書『正月上日受終文祖』，此是何正？

translations.literal: " Yan asked again, "In the Documents, 'On the first day of the first month he received the end from Wen the Ancestor'—which first month is this?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan asked again, "In the Documents, 'On the first day of the first month he received the end from Wen the Ancestor'—which first month is this?

sentences.zh: 」業興對：「此是夏正月。

translations.literal: " Yexing replied, "This is the first month of Xia.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing replied, "This is the first month of the Xia calendar.

sentences.zh: 」衍言何以得知。

translations.literal: " Yan asked how he knew this.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan asked how he knew this.

sentences.zh: 業興曰：「案尚書中候運行篇云『日月營始』，故知夏正。

translations.literal: Yexing said, "According to the Running Phases chapter of the Apocryphal Documents on the Middle Calendars, which says 'The sun and moon set out at the beginning,' one knows it is the Xia first month.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing said, "According to the Running Phases chapter of the Apocryphal Documents on the Middle Calendars, which says 'The sun and moon set out at the beginning,' one knows it is the Xia first month.

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「堯時以何月為正？

translations.literal: " Yan asked again, "In Yao's time, which month served as the first month?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan asked again, "In Yao's time, which month served as the first month?

sentences.zh: 」業興對：「自堯以上，書典不載，實所不知。

translations.literal: " Yexing replied, "From Yao and earlier, the canonical texts do not record this—I truly do not know.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing replied, "From Yao and earlier, the canonical texts do not record this—I truly do not know.

sentences.zh: 」衍又云：「『寅賓出日』，即是正月。

translations.literal: " Yan also said, "'The day is respectfully received at the coming-out of the sun at yin'—that is the first month.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan also said, "'The day is respectfully received at the coming-out of the sun at yin'—that is the first month.

sentences.zh: 『日中星鳥，以殷仲春』，即是二月。

translations.literal: 'When the sun is at mid-heaven and the Star Bird is seen, it is truly mid-spring'—that is the second month.
translations.idiomatic: 'When the sun is at mid-heaven and the Star Bird is seen, it is truly mid-spring'—that is the second month.

sentences.zh: 此出堯典，何得云堯時不知用何正也？

translations.literal: This comes from the Canon of Yao—how can you say that in Yao's time one did not know which month served as the first?
translations.idiomatic: This comes from the Canon of Yao—how can you say that in Yao's time one did not know which month served as the first?

sentences.zh: 」業興對：「雖三正不同，言時節者皆據夏時正月。

translations.literal: " Yexing replied, "Although the Three First Months differ, when speaking of seasons one always takes the Xia calendar's first month as the basis.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing replied, "Although the Three First Months differ, when speaking of seasons one always takes the Xia calendar's first month as the basis.

sentences.zh: 周禮，仲春二月會男女之無夫家者。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, in the second month of mid-spring men and women without spouses are brought together.
translations.idiomatic: In the Rites of Zhou, in the second month of mid-spring men and women without spouses are brought together.

sentences.zh: 雖自周書，月亦夏時。

translations.literal: Although this comes from the Zhou Documents, the month referred to is still the Xia calendar.
translations.idiomatic: Although this comes from the Zhou Documents, the month referred to is still the Xia calendar.

sentences.zh: 堯之日月，亦當如此。

translations.literal: Yao's sun and moon should likewise be so.
translations.idiomatic: Yao's sun and moon should likewise be so.

sentences.zh: 但所見不深，無以辨析明問。

translations.literal: But my reading is not deep enough to analyze and answer your clear question.
translations.idiomatic: But my reading is not deep enough to analyze and answer your clear question.

sentences.zh: 」衍又曰：「禮，原壤之母死，孔子助其沐椁。

translations.literal: " Yan also said, "In the Ritual Records, when Yuan Rang's mother died, Confucius helped him prepare the bathing and coffining.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan also said, "In the Ritual Records, when Yuan Rang's mother died, Confucius helped him prepare the bathing and coffining.

sentences.zh: 原壤叩木而歌曰：『久矣夫，予之不託於音也。

translations.literal: Yuan Rang knocked on the coffin board and sang, 'Long has it been since I have not entrusted myself to music.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Rang knocked on the coffin board and sang, 'Long has it been since I have not entrusted myself to music.

sentences.zh: [11]狸首之班然，執女手之卷然。

translations.literal: [11] Like the spotted pattern of an otter's head, curled as a woman's hand.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Like the spotted pattern of an otter's head, curled as a woman's hand.

sentences.zh: 』孔子聖人，而與原壤為友？

translations.literal: ' Confucius was a sage—yet he befriended Yuan Rang?
translations.idiomatic: ' Confucius was a sage—yet he befriended Yuan Rang?

sentences.zh: 」業興對：「孔子即自解，言親者不失其為親，故者不失其為故。

translations.literal: " Yexing replied, "Confucius himself explained that kin do not cease to be kin, nor do old acquaintances cease to be old acquaintances.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing replied, "Confucius himself explained that kin do not cease to be kin, nor do old acquaintances cease to be old acquaintances.

sentences.zh: 」又問：「原壤何處人？

translations.literal: " He asked again, "Where was Yuan Rang from?
translations.idiomatic: " He asked again, "Where was Yuan Rang from?

sentences.zh: 」業興對曰：「鄭注云：原壤，孔子幼少之舊。

translations.literal: " Yexing replied, "Zheng Xuan's commentary says: Yuan Rang was an old friend from Confucius's youth.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing replied, "Zheng Xuan's commentary says: Yuan Rang was an old friend from Confucius's youth.

sentences.zh: 故是魯人。

translations.literal: Therefore he was a man of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore he was a man of Lu.

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「孔子聖人，所存必可法。

translations.literal: " Yan asked again, "Confucius was a sage—surely what he preserved is worthy of emulation.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan asked again, "Confucius was a sage—surely what he preserved is worthy of emulation.

sentences.zh: 原壤不孝，有逆人倫，何以存故舊之小節，廢不孝之大罪？

translations.literal: Yuan Rang was unfilial and violated human relations—why preserve a small point of old friendship and set aside the great crime of unfiliality?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Rang was unfilial and violated human relations—why preserve a small point of old friendship and set aside the great crime of unfiliality?

sentences.zh: 」業興對曰：「原壤所行，事自彰著。

translations.literal: " Yexing replied, "Yuan Rang's conduct speaks for itself and is manifest.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing replied, "Yuan Rang's conduct speaks for itself and is manifest.

sentences.zh: 幼少之交，非是今始，既無大故，何容棄之？

translations.literal: The friendship of youth did not begin only now—there was no grave cause; how could it be abandoned?
translations.idiomatic: The friendship of youth did not begin only now—there was no grave cause; how could it be abandoned?

sentences.zh: 孔子深敦故舊之義，於理無失。

translations.literal: Confucius deeply honored the meaning of old friendship—there is no fault in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius deeply honored the meaning of old friendship—there is no fault in principle.

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「孔子聖人，何以書原壤之事，垂法萬代？

translations.literal: " Yan asked again, "Confucius was a sage—why record the affair of Yuan Rang and hand down a model for ten thousand generations?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan asked again, "Confucius was a sage—why record the affair of Yuan Rang and hand down a model for ten thousand generations?

sentences.zh: 」業興對曰：「此是後人所錄，非孔子自制。

translations.literal: " Yexing replied, "This was recorded by later men—it was not composed by Confucius himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing replied, "This was recorded by later men—it was not composed by Confucius himself.

sentences.zh: 猶合葬於防，如此之類，禮記之中動有百數。

translations.literal: Such matters as joint burial at Fang—of this sort there are easily a hundred in the Book of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Such matters as joint burial at Fang—of this sort there are easily a hundred in the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 」衍又問：「易曰太極，是有無？

translations.literal: " Yan asked again, "The Changes says Supreme Polarity—is it being or non-being?
translations.idiomatic: " Yan asked again, "The Changes says Supreme Polarity—is it being or non-being?

sentences.zh: 」業興對：「所傳太極是有，素不玄學，何敢輒酬。」

translations.literal: " Yexing replied, "According to tradition Supreme Polarity is being—I have never studied Dark Learning, so how dare I answer offhand."
translations.idiomatic: " Yexing replied, "According to tradition Supreme Polarity is being—I have never studied Dark Learning, so how dare I answer offhand."

sentences.zh: 業興愛好墳籍，鳩集不已，手自補治，躬加題帖，其家所有，垂將萬卷。

translations.literal: Yexing loved ancient texts, collecting them without cease, personally mending and restoring them and adding title slips with his own hand; his household holdings approached ten thousand scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yexing loved ancient texts and collected them without cease, personally mending and restoring them and adding title slips with his own hand. His household holdings approached ten thousand scrolls.

sentences.zh: 覽讀不息，多有異聞，諸儒服其淵博。

translations.literal: He read incessantly, hearing much that was unusual, and the Confucian scholars admired his profound erudition.
translations.idiomatic: He read incessantly, hearing much that was unusual, and the Confucian scholars admired his profound erudition.

sentences.zh: 性豪俠，重意氣。

translations.literal: By nature he was bold and chivalrous, placing great weight on loyalty and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was bold and chivalrous, placing great weight on loyalty and friendship.

sentences.zh: 人有急難，委之歸命，便能容匿。

translations.literal: When men faced urgent distress and entrusted themselves to him for refuge, he could shelter them.
translations.idiomatic: When men faced urgent distress and entrusted themselves to him for refuge, he could shelter them.

sentences.zh: 與其好合，傾身無吝。

translations.literal: With those he favored he was wholeheartedly generous without stint.
translations.idiomatic: With those he favored he was wholeheartedly generous without stint.

sentences.zh: 若有相乖忤，便即疵毀，乃至聲色，加以謗罵。

translations.literal: If there was friction, he would immediately find fault and pick at them, even raising his voice and adding slander and abuse.
translations.idiomatic: If there was friction, he would immediately find fault and pick at them, even raising his voice and adding slander and abuse.

sentences.zh: 性又躁隘，至於論難之際，高聲攘振，無儒者之風。

translations.literal: His nature was also rash and narrow—during debates he would raise his voice and gesticulate wildly, without the bearing of a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was also rash and narrow—during debates he would raise his voice and gesticulate wildly, without the bearing of a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 每語人云：「但道我好，雖知妄言，故勝道惡。

translations.literal: He often told people, "Just say I'm good—even though you know it is false talk, it still beats saying I'm bad.
translations.idiomatic: He often told people, "Just say I'm good—even though you know it is false talk, it still beats saying I'm bad.

sentences.zh: 」務進忌前，不顧後患，時人以此惡之。

translations.literal: " He strove to advance, resented those ahead of him, and gave no thought to later troubles; people at the time hated him for this.
translations.idiomatic: " He strove to advance, resented those ahead of him, and gave no thought to later troubles; people at the time hated him for this.

sentences.zh: 至於學術精微，當時莫及。

translations.literal: As for the subtle depths of learning, no one of the time could match him.
translations.idiomatic: As for the subtle depths of learning, no one of the time could match him.

sentences.zh: 子崇祖，武定中，太尉外兵參軍。

translations.literal: His son Chongzu served as External Troops Aide to the Grand Marshal during the Wuding era.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chongzu served as External Troops Aide to the Grand Marshal during the Wuding era.

sentences.zh: 崇祖弟遵祖，太昌中，業興傳其長子伯以授之。

translations.literal: Chongzu's younger brother Zunzu—in the Taichang era Yexing had his eldest son Bo pass down the transmission and entrusted it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu's younger brother Zunzu—in the Taichang era Yexing had his eldest son Bo pass down the family learning and entrusted it to him.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，例降。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was reduced in rank by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication, he was reduced in rank by precedent.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：古語云：容體不足觀，勇力不足恃，族姓不足道，先祖不足稱，然而顯聞四方，流聲後裔者，其惟學乎。

translations.literal: The historiographer remarks: An ancient saying runs, "Physique is not worth looking at, courage and strength are not worth relying on, clan and surname are not worth mentioning, and forebears are not worth boasting of—yet to be renowned in all directions and leave a name to posterity, is it not through learning?"
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer remarks: An ancient saying runs, "Physique is not worth looking at, courage and strength are not worth relying on, clan and surname are not worth mentioning, and forebears are not worth boasting of—yet to be renowned in all directions and leave a name to posterity, is it not through learning?"

sentences.zh: 信哉斯言也。

translations.literal: How true these words are!
translations.idiomatic: How true these words are!

sentences.zh: 梁越之徒，篤志不倦，自求諸己，遂能聞道下風，稱珍席上，或聚徒千百，或服冕乘軒，咸稽古之力也。

translations.literal: Men such as Liang Yue devoted themselves tirelessly, seeking within themselves, and were thus able to hear the Way and attend lectures from below, to be prized at the lectern; some gathered hundreds or thousands of disciples, others wore regalia and rode in chariots—all owed to the power of studying antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Liang Yue devoted themselves tirelessly, seeking within themselves, and were thus able to hear the Way and attend lectures from below, to be prized at the lectern. Some gathered hundreds or thousands of disciples, others wore regalia and rode in chariots—all owed to the power of studying antiquity.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 魏書卷八十四 諸本目錄此卷注「不全」，卷末有宋人校語云：「高氏小史儒林傳無刁沖、盧景裕、李同軌三人，史目錄皆有之。

translations.literal: Book of Wei, juan 84: the table of contents in various editions notes this juan as "incomplete." At the end of the juan is a Song-dynasty collation note that reads, "The Confucian Scholars section of Gao's Brief History lacks the three men Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, and Li Tonggui, but the History's table of contents lists them all.
translations.idiomatic: Book of Wei, juan 84: the table of contents in various editions notes this juan as "incomplete." At the end of the juan is a Song-dynasty collation note that reads, "The Confucian Scholars section of Gao's Brief History lacks the three men Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, and Li Tonggui, but the History's table of contents lists them all.

sentences.zh: 此卷刁沖、盧景裕傳全錄北史，非魏收書，史臣論亦出北史，北史全用隋書傳論。

translations.literal: The biographies of Diao Chong and Lu Jingyu in this juan are copied entirely from the History of the Northern Dynasties and are not from Wei Shou's book; the historiographer's comment also comes from the Northern History, which in turn wholly adopts the biographical commentaries of the History of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: The biographies of Diao Chong and Lu Jingyu in this juan are copied entirely from the History of the Northern Dynasties and are not from Wei Shou's book. The historiographer's comment also comes from the Northern History, which in turn wholly adopts the biographical commentaries of the History of the Sui.

sentences.zh: 」殿本以校語入考證，開頭一句又改成「魏收書儒林傳亡，用高氏小史補之」。

translations.literal: " The Palace Edition incorporated the collation note into its textual verification, and changed the opening sentence to "Wei Shou's Confucian Scholars section is lost; it was supplemented from Gao's Brief History."
translations.idiomatic: " The Palace Edition incorporated the collation note into its textual verification and changed the opening sentence to "Wei Shou's Confucian Scholars section is lost; it was supplemented from Gao's Brief History."

sentences.zh: 按此卷常爽、刁沖、盧景裕、李同軌四傳，北史卷八一儒林傳所無。

translations.literal: According to this, the four biographies of Chang Shuang, Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, and Li Tonggui in this juan are absent from the Confucian Scholars section in juan 81 of the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: According to this, the four biographies of Chang Shuang, Diao Chong, Lu Jingyu, and Li Tonggui in this juan are absent from the Confucian Scholars section in juan 81 of the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 常爽，北史卷四二有專傳，刁沖附卷二六刁雍傳，盧景裕附卷三０盧同傳，李同軌附卷三三李義深傳。

translations.literal: Chang Shuang has a separate biography in juan 42 of the Northern History; Diao Chong is appended to the biography of Diao Yong in juan 26; Lu Jingyu is appended to the biography of Lu Tong in juan 30; Li Tonggui is appended to the biography of Li Yishen in juan 33.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Shuang has a separate biography in juan 42 of the Northern History. Diao Chong is appended to the biography of Diao Yong in juan 26; Lu Jingyu is appended to the biography of Lu Tong in juan 30; Li Tonggui is appended to the biography of Li Yishen in juan 33.

sentences.zh: 今檢此卷常爽傳也全同北史，宋人漏舉。

translations.literal: On examination, the biography of Chang Shuang in this juan is also identical to the Northern History—the Song editors omitted mention of it.
translations.idiomatic: On examination, the biography of Chang Shuang in this juan is also identical to the Northern History—the Song editors omitted mention of it.

sentences.zh: 李同軌則魏書本已附卷三六李順傳，與此卷同軌傳幾乎全同，一人二傳，實為重出

translations.literal: Li Tonggui, meanwhile, was already appended to the biography of Li Shun in juan 36 of the original Book of Wei; the Tonggui biography in this juan is nearly identical—one man with two biographies, a true duplication
translations.idiomatic: Li Tonggui, meanwhile, was already appended to the biography of Li Shun in juan 36 of the original Book of Wei. The Tonggui biography in this juan is nearly identical—one man with two biographies, a true duplication

sentences.zh: 〈北史同軌傳較簡〉

translations.literal: 〈The Northern History Tonggui biography is briefer〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈The Northern History Tonggui biography is briefer〉

sentences.zh: 其他諸傳，凡北史儒林傳所有諸人都比北史詳備。

translations.literal: The other biographies—all the men who appear in the Northern History's Confucian Scholars section—are more detailed here than in the Northern History.
translations.idiomatic: The other biographies—all the men who appear in the Northern History's Confucian Scholars section—are more detailed here than in the Northern History.

sentences.zh: 其中徐遵明傳，北史多出勒索學生事，李業興傳多出語音不正和與孫騰、邢子才對答語，當是北史據其他材料增入，非魏書原文所有。

translations.literal: Among them, the biography of Xu Zunming in the Northern History adds the affair of extorting students; the biography of Li Yexing adds incorrect pronunciation and exchanges with Sun Teng and Xing Zicai—these were likely added by the Northern History from other materials and are not in the original Book of Wei text.
translations.idiomatic: Among them, the biography of Xu Zunming in the Northern History adds the affair of extorting students. The biography of Li Yexing adds incorrect pronunciation and exchanges with Sun Teng and Xing Zicai—these were likely added by the Northern History from other materials and are not in the original Book of Wei text.

sentences.zh: 傳序也像是北史傳序敍魏事一段所本。

translations.literal: The preface to the biographies also appears to be the source for the Northern History's preface section narrating Wei affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The preface to the biographies also appears to be the source for the Northern History's preface section narrating Wei affairs.

sentences.zh: 據上述情況，除常、刁、盧三傳及史論外，似皆魏書原文。
